1.92.d: एता उ तया उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमञ्जते | निष्क्र्ण्वाना आयुधानीव धर्ष्णवः परति गावोऽरुषीर्यन्ति मातरः ||
1.92.e: THESE Dawns have raised their banner; in the eastern half of the mid-air they spread abroad their shining light.  Like heroes who prepare their weapons for the war, onward they come bright red in hue, the Mother Cows.

1.92.d: उदपप्तन्नरुणा भानवो वर्था सवायुजो अरुषीर्गा अयुक्सत | अक्रन्नुषासो वयुनानि पूर्वथा रुशन्तं भानुमरुषीरशिश्रयुः ||
1.92.e: Readily have the purple beams of light shot up; the Red Cows have they harnessed, easy to be yoked.  The Dawns have brought distinct perception as before: red-hued, they have attained their fulgent brilliancy.

1.92.d: अर्चन्ति नारीरपसो न विष्टिभिः समानेन योजनेना परावतः | इषं वहन्तीः सुक्र्ते सुदानवे विश्वेदह यजमानाय सुन्वते ||
1.92.e: They sing their song like women active in their tasks, along their common path hither from far away,  Bringing refreshment to the liberal devotee, yea, all things to the worshipper who pours the juice.

1.92.d: अधि पेशांसि वपते नर्तूरिवापोर्णुते वक्ष उस्रेव बर्जहम | जयोतिर्विश्वस्मै भुवनाय कर्ण्वती गावो न वरजं वयुषा आवर्तमः ||
1.92.e: She, like a dancer, puts her broidered garments on: as a cow yields her udder so she bares her breast.  Creating light for all the world of life, the Dawn hath laid the darkness open as the cows their stall.

1.92.d: परत्यर्ची रुशदस्या अदर्शि वि तिष्ठते बाधते कर्ष्णमभ्वम | सवरुं न पेशो विदथेष्वञ्जञ्चित्रं दिवो दुहिता भानुमश्रेत ||
1.92.e: We have beheld the brightness of her shining; it spreads and drives away the darksome monster.  Like tints that deck the Post at sacrifices, Heaven's Daughter hath attained her wondrous splendour.

1.92.d: अतारिष्म तमसस पारमस्योषा उछन्ती वयुना कर्णोति | शरिये छन्दो न समयते विभाती सुप्रतीका सौमनसायाजीगः ||
1.92.e: We have o’erpast the limit of this darkness; Dawn breaking forth again brings clear perception.  She like a flatterer smiles in light for glory, and fair of face hath wakened to rejoice us.

1.92.d: भास्वती नेत्री सून्र्तानां दिव सतवे दुहिता गोतमेभिः | परजावतो नर्वतो अश्वबुध्यानुषो गोग्रानुप मासि वाजान ||
1.92.e: The Gotamas have praised Heaven's radiant Daughter, the leader of the charm of pleasant voices.  Dawn, thou conferrest on us strength with offspring and men, conspicuous with kine and horses.

1.92.d: उषस्तमश्यां यशसं सुवीरं दासप्रवर्गं रयिमश्वबुध्यम | सुदंससा शरवसा या विभासि वाजप्रसूता सुभगे बर्हन्तम ||
1.92.e: O thou who shinest forth in wondrous glory, urged onward by thy strength, auspicious Lady,  Dawn, may I gain that wealth, renowned and ample, in brave sons, troops of slaves, far-famed for horses.

1.92.d: विश्वानि देवी भुवनाभिचक्ष्या परतीची चक्षुरुर्विया वि भाति | विश्वं जीवं चरसे बोधयन्ती विश्वस्य वाचमविदन मनायोः ||
1.92.e: Bending her looks on all the world, the Goddess shines, widely spreading with her bright eye westward.  Waking to motion every living creature, she understands the voice of each adorer.

1.92.d: पुनः-पुनर्जायमाना पुराणी समानं वर्णमभि शुम्भमाना | शवघ्नीव कर्त्नुर्विज आमिनाना मर्तस्य देवी जरयन्त्यायुः ||
1.92.e: Ancient of days, again again born newly, decking her beauty with the self-same raiment.  The Goddess wastes away the life of mortals, like a skilled hunter cutting birds in pieces.

1.92.d: वयूर्ण्वती दिवो अन्तानबोध्यप सवसारं सनुतर्युयोति | परमिनती मनुष्या युगानि योषा जारस्य चक्षसा वि भाति ||
1.92.e: She hath appeared discovering heaven's borders: to the far distance she drives off her Sister.  Diminishing the days of human creatures, the Lady shines with all her lover's splendour.

1.92.d: पशून न चित्रा सुभगा परथाना सिन्धुर्न कषोद उर्विया वयश्वैत | अमिनती दैव्यानि वरतानि सूर्यस्य चेति रश्मिभिर्द्र्शाना ||
1.92.e: The bright, the blessed One shines forth extending her rays like kine, as a flood rolls his waters.  Never transgressing the divine commandments, she is beheld visible with the sunbeams.

1.92.d: उषस्तच्चित्रमा भरास्मभ्यं वाजिनीवति | येन तोकंच तनयं च धामहे ||
1.92.e: O Dawn enriched with ample wealth, bestow on us the wondrous gift  Wherewith we may support children and children's sons.

1.92.d: उषो अद्येह गोमत्यश्वावति विभावरि | रेवदस्मे वयुछ सून्र्तावति ||
1.92.e: Thou radiant mover of sweet sounds, with wealth of horses and of kine  Shine thou on us this day, O Dawn auspiciously.

1.92.d: युक्ष्वा हि वाजिनीवत्यश्वानद्यारुणानुषः | अथा नोविश्वा सौभगान्या वह ||
1.92.e: O Dawn enriched with holy rites, yoke to thy car thy purple steeds,  And then bring thou unto us all felicities.

1.92.d: अश्विना वर्तिरस्मदा गोमद दस्रा हिरण्यवत | अर्वाग रथं समनसा नि यछतम ||
1.92.e: O Aśvins wonderful in act, do ye unanimous direct  Your chariot to our home wealthy in kine and gold.

1.92.d: यावित्था शलोकमा दिवो जयोतिर्जनाय चक्रथुः | आ नूर्जं वहतमश्विना युवम ||
1.92.e: Ye who brought down the hymn from heaven, a light that giveth light to man,  Do ye, O Aśvins, bring strength hither unto us.

1.92.d: एह देवा मयोभुवा दस्रा हिरण्यवर्तनी | उषर्बुधो वहन्तु सोमपीतये ||
1.92.e: Hither may they who wake at dawn bring, to drink Soma both the Gods  Health-givers Wonder-Workers, borne on paths of gold.

1.93.d: अग्नीषोमाविमं सु मे शर्णुतं वर्षणा हवम | परति सूक्तानि हर्यतं भवतं दाशुषे मयः ||
1.93.e: AGNI and Soma, mighty Pair, graciously hearken to my call,  Accept in friendly wise my hymn, and prosper him who offers gifts.

1.93.d: अग्नीषोमा यो अद्य वामिदं वचः सपर्यति | तस्मै धत्तं सुवीर्यं गवां पोषं सवश्व्यम ||
1.93.e: The man who honours you to-day, Agni and Soma, with this hymn,  Bestow on him heroic strength, increase of kine, and noble steeds.

1.93.d: अग्नीषोमा य आहुतिं यो वां दाशाद धविष्क्र्तिम | स परजया सुवीर्यं विश्वमायुर्व्यश्नवत ||
1.93.e: The man who offers holy oil and burnt oblations unto you,  Agni and Soma, shall enjoy great strength, with offspring, all his life.

1.93.d: अग्नीषोमा चेति तद वीर्यं वां यदमुष्णीतमवसं पणिं गाः | अवातिरतं बर्सयस्य शेषो.अविन्दतं जयोतिरेकं बहुभ्यः ||
1.93.e: Agni and Soma, famed is that your. prowess wherewith ye stole the kine, his food, from Paṇi.  Ye caused the brood of Bṛsaya to perish; ye found the light, the single light for many.

1.93.d: युवमेतानि दिवि रोचनान्यग्निश्च सोम सक्रतू अधत्तम | युवं सिन्धून्रभिशस्तेरवद्यादग्नीषोमावमुञ्चतं गर्भीतान ||
1.93.e: Agni and Soma, joined in operation ye have set up the shining lights in heaven.  From curse and from reproach, Agni and Soma, ye freed the rivers that were bound in fetters.

1.93.d: आन्यं दिवो मातरिश्वा जभारामथ्नादन्यं परि शयेनोद्रेः | अग्नीषोमा बरह्मणा वाव्र्धानोरुं यज्ञाय चक्रथुरु लोकम ||
1.93.e: One of you Mātariśvan brought from heaven, the Falcon rent the other from the mountain.  Strengthened by holy prayer Agni and Soma have made us ample room for sacrificing.

1.93.d: अग्नीषोमा हविषः परस्थितस्य वीतं हर्यतं वर्षणा जुषेथाम | सुशर्माणा सववसा हि भूतमथा धत्तं यजमानाय शं योः ||
1.93.e: Taste, Agni, Soma, this prepared oblation; accept it, Mighty Ones, and let it please you.  Vouchsafe us good protection and kind favour: grant to the sacrificer health and riches.

1.93.d: यो अग्नीषोमा हविषा सपर्याद देवद्रीचा मनसा यो घर्तेन | तस्य वरतं रक्षतं पातमंहसो विशे जनाय महिशर्म यछतम ||
1.93.e: Whoso with oil and poured oblation honours, with God-devoted heart, Agni and Soma,—  Protect his sacrifice, preserve him from distress, grant to the sacrificer great felicity.

1.93.d: अग्नीषोमा सवेदसा सहूती वनतं गिरः | सं देवत्रा बभूवथुः ||
1.93.e: Invoked together, mates in wealth, Agni-Soma, accept our hymns:  Together be among the Gods.

1.93.d: अग्नीषोमावनेन वां यो वां घर्तेन दाशति | तस्मै दीदयतं बर्हत ||
1.93.e: Agni and Soma, unto him who worships you with holy oil  Shine forth an ample recompense.

1.93.d: अग्नीषोमाविमानि नो युवं हव्या जुजोषतम | आ यातमुपनः सचा ||
1.93.e: Agni and Soma, be ye pleased with these oblations brought to you,  And come, together, nigh to us.

1.93.d: अग्नीषोमा पिप्र्तमर्वतो न आ पयायन्तामुस्रिया हव्यसूदः | अस्मे बलानि मघवत्सु धत्तं कर्णुतं नो अध्वरं शरुष्टिमन्तम ||
1.93.e: Agni and Soma, cherish well our horses, and let our cows be fat who yield oblations.  Grant power to us and to our wealthy patrons, and cause our holy rites to be successful.

1.94.d: इमं सतोममर्हते जातवेदसे रथमिव सं महेमा मनीषया | भद्रा हि नः परमतिरस्य संसद्यग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ||
1.94.e: FOR Jātavedas worthy of our praise will we frame with our mind this eulogy as ’twere a car.  For good, in his assembly, is this care of ours. Let us not, in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: यस्मै तवमायजसे स साधत्यनर्वा कषेति दधते सुवीर्यम | स तूताव नैनमश्नोत्यंहतिरग्ने ... ||
1.94.e: The man for whom thou sacrificest prospereth, dwelleth without a foe, gaineth heroic might.  He waxeth strong, distress never approacheth him. Let us not, in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: शकेम तवा समिधं साधया धियस्त्वे देवा हविरदन्त्याहुतम | तवमादित्याना वह तान हयुश्मस्यग्ने ... ||
1.94.e: May we have power to kindle thee. Fulfil our thoughts. In thee the Gods eat the presented offering,  Bring hither the Ādityas, for we long for them. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: भरामेध्मं कर्णवामा हवींषि ते चितयन्तः पर्वणा-पर्वणा वयम | जीवातवे परतरं साधया धियो.अग्ने ... ||
1.94.e: We will bring fuel and prepare burnt offerings, reminding thee at each successive festival.  Fulfil our thought that so we may prolong our lives. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: विशां गोपा अस्य चरन्ति जन्तवो दविपच्च यदुत चतुष्पदक्तुभिः | चित्रः परकेत उषसो महानस्य अग्ने ... ||
1.94.e: His ministers move forth, the guardians of the folk, protecting quadruped and biped with their rays.  Mighty art thou, the wondrous herald of the Dawn. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: तवमध्वर्युरुत होतासि पूर्व्यः परशास्ता पोता जनुषा पुरोहितः | विश्वा विद्वानार्त्विज्या धीर पुष्यस्यग्ने .. . ||
1.94.e: Thou art Presenter and the chief Invoker, thou Director, Purifier, great High Priest by birth.  Knowing all priestly work thou perfectest it, Sage. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: यो विश्वतः सुप्रतीकः सद्रंं असि दूरे चित सन तळिदिवाति रोचसे | रात्र्याश्चिदन्धो अति देव पश्यस्यग्ने ... ||
1.94.e: Lovely of form art thou, alike on every side; though far, thou shinest brightly as if close at hand.  O God, thou seest through even the dark of night. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: पूर्वो देवा भवतु सुन्वतो रथो.अस्माकं शंसो अभ्यस्तु दूढ्यः | तदा जानीतोत पुष्यता वचो.अग्ने ... ||
1.94.e: Gods, foremost be his car who pours libations out, and let our hymn prevail o’er evil-hearted men.  Attend to this our speech and make it prosper well. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: वधैर्दुःशंसानप दूढ्यो जहि दूरे वा ये अन्ति वा के चिदत्रिणः | अथा यज्ञाय गर्णते सुगं कर्ध्यग्ने ... ||
1.94.e: Smite with thy weapons those of evil speech and thought, devouring demons, whether near or tar away.  Then to the singer give free way for sacrifice. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: यदयुक्था अरुषा रोहिता रथे वातजूता वर्षभस्येव तेरवः | आदिन्वसि वनिनो धूमकेतुनाग्ने ... ||
1.94.e: When to thy chariot thou hadst yoked two red steeds and two ruddy steeds, wind-sped, thy roar was like a bull's.  Thou with smoke-bannered flame attackest forest trees. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: अध सवनादुत बिभ्युः पतत्रिणो दरप्सा यत ते यवसादो वयस्थिरन | सुगं तत ते तावकेभ्यो रथेभ्यो.अग्ने ... ||
1.94.e: Then at thy roar the very birds are terrified, when, eating-up the grass, thy sparks fly forth abroad.  Then is it easy for thee and thy car to pass. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: अयं मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धायसे.अवयातां मरुतां हेळो अद्भुतः | मर्ळा सु नो भूत्वेषां मनः पुनरग्ने ... ||
1.94.e: He hath the Power to soothe Mitra and Varuṇa: wonderful is the Maruts’ wrath when they descend.  Be gracious; let their hearts he turned to us again. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: देवो देवानामसि मित्रो अद्भुतो वसुर्वसूनामसि चारुरध्वरे | शर्मन सयाम तव सप्रथस्तमे.अग्ने ... ||
1.94.e: Thou art a God, thou art the wondrous Friend of Gods, the Vasu of the Vasus, fair in sacrifice.  Under, thine own most wide protection may we dwell. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: तत ते भद्रं यत समिद्धः सवे दमे सोमाहुतो जरसे मर्ळयत्तमः | दधासि रत्नं दरविणं च दाशुषे.अग्ने ... ||
1.94.e: This is thy grace that, kindled in thine own abode, invoked with Soma thou soundest forth most benign,  Thou givest wealth and treasure to the worshipper. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.

1.94.d: यस्मै तवं सुद्रविणो ददाशो.अनागास्त्वमदिते सर्वताता | यं भद्रेण शवसा चोदयासि परजावता राधसा ते सयाम ||
1.94.e: To whom thou, Lord of goodly riches, grantest freedom from every sin with perfect wholeness,  Whom with good strength thou  quickenest  , with children and wealth—may we be they, Eternal Being.

1.94.d: स तवमग्ने सौभगत्वस्य विद्वानस्माकमायुः पर तिरेहदेव | तन नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहन्तामदितिः सिन्धुः पर्थिवी उत दयौः ||
1.94.e: Such, Agni, thou who knowest all good fortune, God, lengthen here the days of our existence.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.95.d: दवे वीरूपे चरतः सवर्थे अन्यान्या वत्समुप धापयेते | हरिरन्यस्यां भवति सवधावाञ्छुक्रो अन्यस्यां दद्र्शे सुवर्चाः ||
1.95.e: To fair goals travel Two unlike in semblance: each in succession nourishes an infant.  One bears a Godlike Babe of golden colour; bright and fair-shining, is he with the other.

1.95.d: दशेमं तवष्टुर्जनयन्त गर्भमतन्द्रासो युवतयो विभ्र्त्रम | तिग्मानीकं सवयशसं जनेषु विरोचमानं परि षीं नयन्ति ||
1.95.e: Tvaṣṭar's ten daughters, vigilant and youthful, produced this Infant borne to sundry quarters.  They bear around him whose long flames are pointed, fulgent among mankind with native splendour.

1.95.d: तरीणि जाना परि भूषन्त्यस्य समुद्र एकं दिव्येकमप्सु | पूर्वामनु पर दिशं पार्थिवानां रतून परशासद विदधावनुष्ठु ||
1.95.e: Three several places of his birth they honour, in mid-air, in the heaven, and in the waters.  Governing in the east of earthly regions, the seasons hath he stablished in their order.

1.95.d: क इमं वो निण्यमा चिकेत वत्सो मातॄर्जनयत सवधाभिः | बह्वीनां गर्भो अपसामुपस्थान महान कविर्निश्चरति सवधावान ||
1.95.e: Who of you knows this secret One? The Infant by his own nature hath brought forth his Mothers.  The germ of many, from the waters' bosom he goes forth, wise and great, of Godlike nature.

1.95.d: आविष्ट्यो वर्धते चारुरासु जिह्मानामूर्ध्वः सवयशा उपस्थे | उभे तवष्टुर्बिभ्यतुर्जायमानात परतीची सिंहम्प्रति जोषयेते ||
1.95.e: Visible, fair, he grows in native brightness uplifted in the lap of waving waters.  When he was born both Tvaṣṭar's worlds were frightened: they turn to him and reverence the Lion.

1.95.d: उभे भद्रे जोषयेते न मेने गावो न वाश्रा उप तस्थुरेवैः | स दक्षाणां दक्षपतिर्बभूवाञ्जन्ति यं दक्षिणतो हविर्भिः ||
1.95.e: The Two auspicious Ones, like women, tend him: like lowing cows they seek him in their manner.  He is the Lord of Might among the mighty; him, on the right, they balm with their oblations.

1.95.d: उद यंयमीति सवितेव बाहू उभे सिचौ यतते भीम रञ्जन | उच्छुक्रमत्कमजते सिमस्मान नवा मात्र्भ्यो वसना जहाति ||
1.95.e: Like Savitar his arms with might he stretches; awful, he strives grasping the world's two borders.  He forces out from all a brilliant vesture, yea, from his Mothers draws he forth new raiment.

1.95.d: तवेषं रूपं कर्णुत उत्तरं यत सम्प्र्ञ्चानः सदने गोभिरद्भिः | कविर्बुध्नं परि मर्म्र्ज्यते धीः सा देवताता समितिर्बभूव ||
1.95.e: He makes him a most noble form of splendour, decking him in his home with milk and waters.  The Sage adorns the depths of air with wisdom: this is the meeting where the Gods are worshipped.

1.95.d: उरु ते जरयः पर्येति बुध्नं विरोचमानं महिषस्य धाम | विश्वेभिरग्ने सवयशोभिरिद्धो.अदब्धेभिः पायुभिः पाह्यस्मान ||
1.95.e: Wide through the firmament spreads forth triumphant the far-resplendent strength of thee the Mighty.  Kindled by us do thou preserve us, Agni, with all thy self-bright undiminished succours.

1.95.d: धन्वन सरोतः कर्णुते गातुमूर्मिं शुक्रैरूर्मिभिरभिनक्षति कषाम | विश्वा सनानि जठरेषु धत्ते.अन्तर्नवासु चरति परसूषु ||
1.95.e: In dry spots he makes stream, and course, and torrent, and inundates the earth with floods that glisten.  All ancient things within his maw he gathers, and moves among the new fresh-sprouting grasses.

1.95.d: एवा नो अग्ने समिधा वर्धानो रेवत पावक शरवसे वि भाहि | तन नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहन्ताम अदितिः सिन्धुः पर्थ्विवी उतो दयौः ||
1.95.e: Fed with our fuel, purifying Agni, so blaze to us auspiciously for glory.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.96.d: स परत्नथा सहसा जायमानः सद्यः काव्यानि बळ अधत्त विश्वा | अपश्च मित्रं धिषणा च साधन देवा अग्निन्धारयन दरविणोदाम ||
1.96.e: HE in the ancient way by strength engendered, lo! straight hath taken to himself all wisdom.  The waters and the bowl have made him friendly. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.

1.96.d: स पूर्वया निविदा कव्यतायोरिमाः परजा अजनयन मनूनाम | विवस्वता चक्षसा दयामपश्च देवा अ. ध. द. ||
1.96.e: At Āyu's ancient call he by his wisdom gave all this progeny of men their being,  And, by refulgent light, heaven and the waters. The Gods possessed the wealth. bestowing Agni.

1.96.d: तमीळत परथमं यज्ञसाधं विश आरीराहुतं रञ्जसानम | ऊर्जः पुत्रं भरतं सर्प्रदानुं देवा ... ||
1.96.e: Praise him, ye Āryan folk, as chief performer of sacrifice adored and ever toiling,  Well-tended, Son of Strength, the Constant Giver. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.

1.96.d: स मातरिश्वा पुरुवारपुष्टिर्विदद गातुं तनयाय सवर्वित | विशां गोपा जनिता रोदस्योर्देवा ... ||
1.96.e: That Mātariśvan rich in wealth and treasure, light-winner, finds a pathway for his offspring.  Guard of our folk, Father of earth and heaven. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.

1.96.d: नक्तोषासा वर्णमामेम्याने धापयेते शिशुमेकं समीची | दयावाक्षामा रुक्मो अन्तर्वि भाति देवा ... ||
1.96.e: Night and Dawn, changing each the other's colour, meeting together suckle one same Infant:  Golden between the heaven and earth he shineth. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.

1.96.d: रायो बुध्नः संगमनो वसूनां यज्ञस्य केतुर्मन्मसाधनो वेः | अम्र्तत्वं रक्षमाणास एनं देवा ... ||
1.96.e: Root of wealth, gathering-place of treasures, banner of sacrifice, who grants the suppliant's wishes:  Preserving him as their own life immortal, the Gods possessed the wealth-bestowing Agni.

1.96.d: नू च पुरा च सदनं रयीणां जातस्य च जायमानस्य च कषाम | सतश्च गोपां भवतश्च भूरेर्देवा ... ||
1.96.e: Now and of old the home of wealth, the mansion of what is born and what was born aforetime,  Guard of what is and what will be hereafter,—the Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.

1.96.d: दरविणोदा दरविणसस्तुरस्य दरविणोदाः सनरस्य पर यंसत | दरविणोदा वीरवतीमिषं नो दरविणोदा रसते दीर्घमायुः ||
1.96.e: May the Wealth-Giver grant us conquering riches; may the Wealth-Giver grant us wealth with heroes.  May the Wealth-Giver grant us food with offspring, and length of days may the Wealth-Giver send us.

1.96.d: एवा नो अग्ने समिधा वर्धानो रेवत पावक शरवसे वि भाहि ||
1.96.e: Fed with our fuel, purifying Agni, so blaze to us auspiciously for glory.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.96.d: तन नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहन्ताम अदितिः सिन्धुः पर्थ्विवी उतो दयौः ||

1.97.d: अप नः शोशुचदघमग्ने शुशुग्ध्या रयिम | अप नः शोशुचदघम ||
1.97.e: CHASING with light our sin away, O Agni, shine thou wealth on us.  May his light chase our sin away.

1.97.d: सुक्षेत्रिया सुगातुया वसूया च यजामहे | अप ... ||
1.97.e: For goodly fields, for pleasant homes, for wealth we sacrifice to thee.  May his light chase our sin away.

1.97.d: पर यद भन्दिष्ठ एषां परास्माकासश्च सूरयः | अप... ||
1.97.e: Best praiser of all these be he; foremost, our chiefs who sacrifice.  May his light chase our sin away.

1.97.d: पर यत ते अग्ने सूरयो जायेमहि पर ते वयम | अप ... ||
1.97.e: So that thy worshippers and we, thine, Agni, in our sons may live.  May his light chase our sin away.

1.97.d: पर यदग्नेः सहस्वतो विश्वतो यन्ति भानवः | अप ... ||
1.97.e: As ever-conquering Agni's beams of splendour go to every side,  May his light chase our sin away.

1.97.d: तवं हि विश्वतोमुख विश्वतः परिभूरसि | अप ... ||
1.97.e: To every side thy face is turned, thou art triumphant everywhere.  May his light chase our sin away.

1.97.d: दविषो नो विश्वतोमुखाति नावेव पारय | अप ... ||
1.97.e: O thou whose face looks every way, bear us past foes as in a ship.  May his light chase our sin away.

1.97.d: स नः सिन्धुमिव नावयाति पर्षा सवस्तये | अप ... ||
1.97.e: As in a ship, convey thou us for our advantage o’er the flood.  May his light chase our sin away.

1.98.d: वैश्वानरस्य सुमतौ सयाम राजा हि कं भुवनानामभिश्रीः | इतो जातो विश्वमिदं वि चष्टे वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण ||
1.98.e: STILL in Vaiśvānara's grace may we continue: yea, he is King supreme o’er all things living.  Sprung hence to life upon this All he looketh. Vaiśvānara hath rivalry with Sūrya.

1.98.d: पर्ष्टो दिवि पर्ष्टो अग्निः पर्थिव्यां पर्ष्टो विश्वा ओषधीरा विवेश | वैश्वानरः सहसा पर्ष्टो अग्निः स नो दिवा स रिषः पातु नक्तम ||
1.98.e: Present in heaven, in earth, all-present Agni,—all plants that grow on ground hath he pervaded.  May Agni, may Vaiśvānara with vigour, present, preserve us day and night from foemen.

1.98.d: वैश्वानर तव तत सत्यमस्त्वस्मान रायो मघवानः सचन्ताम | तन नो ... ||
1.98.e: Be this thy truth, Vaiśvānara, to us-ward: let wealth in rich abundance gather round us.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.99.d: जातवेदसे सुनवाम सोममरातीयतो नि दहाति वेदः | स नः पर्षदति दुर्गाणि विश्वा नावेव सिन्धुं दुरितात्यग्निः ||
1.99.e: FOR Jātavedas let us press the Soma: may he consume the wealth of the malignant.  May Agni carry us through all our troubles, through grief as in a boat across the river.

1.100.d: स यो वर्षा वर्ष्ण्येभिः समोका महो दिवः पर्थिव्याश्चसम्राट | सतीनसत्वा हव्यो भरेषु मरुत्वान नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ||
1.100.e: MAY he who hath his home with strength, the Mighty, the King supreme of earth and spacious heaven,  Lord of true power, to he invoked in battles,—may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: यस्यानाप्तः सूर्यस्येव यामो भरे-भरे वर्त्रहा शुष्मो अस्ति | वर्षन्तमः सखिभिः सवेभिरेवैर्म... ||
1.100.e: Whose way is unattainable like Sūrya's: he in each fight is the strong Vṛtra-slayer,  Mightiest with his Friends in his own courses. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: दिवो न यस्य रेतसो दुघानाः पन्थासो यन्ति शवसापरीताः | तरद्द्वेषाः सासहिः पौंस्येभिर्म... ||
1.100.e: Whose paths go forth in their great might resistless, forthmilking, as it were, heaven's genial moisture.  With manly strength triumphant, foe-subduer,—may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: सो अङगिरोभिरङगिरस्तमो भूद वर्षा वर्षभिः सखिभिः सखा सन | रग्मिभिर्र्ग्मी गातुभिर्ज्येष्ठो म... ||
1.100.e: Among Aṅgirases he was the chiefest, a Friend with friends, mighty amid the mighty.  Praiser mid praisers, honoured most of singers. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: स सूनुभिर्न रुद्रेभिर्र्भ्वा नर्षाह्ये सासह्वानमित्रान | सनीळेभिः शरवस्यानि तूर्वन म... ||
1.100.e: Strong with the Rudras as with his own children, in manly battle conquering his foemen '  With his close comrades doing deeds of glory,—may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: स मन्युमीः समदनस्य कर्तास्माकेभिर्न्र्भिः सूर्यं सनत | अस्मिन्नहन सत्पतिः पुरुहूतो म... ||
1.100.e: Humbler of pride, exciter of the conflict, the Lord of heroes, God invoked of many,  May he this day gain with our men the sunlight. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: तमूतयो रणयञ्छूरसातौ तं कषेमस्य कषितयः कर्ण्वत तराम | स विश्वस्य करुणस्येश एको म... ||
1.100.e: His help hath made him cheerer in the battle, the folk have made him guardian of their comfort.  Sole Lord is he of every holy service. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: तमप्सन्त शवस उत्सवेषु नरो नरमवसे तं धनाय | सो अन्धे चित तमसि जयोतिर्विदन म... ||
1.100.e: To him the Hero, on high days of prowess, heroes for help and booty shall betake them.  He hath found light even in the blinding darkness. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: स सव्येन यमति वराधतश्चित स दक्षिणे संग्र्भीता कर्तानि | स कीरिणा चित सनिता धनानि म... ||
1.100.e: He with his left hand checketh even the mighty, and with his right hand gathereth up the booty.  Even with the humble he acquireth riches. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: स गरामेभिः सनिता स रथेभिर्विदे विश्वाभिः कर्ष्टिभिर्न्वद्य | स पौंस्येभिरभिभूरशस्तीर्म... ||
1.100.e: With hosts on foot and cars he winneth treasures: well is he known this day by all the people.  With manly might he conquereth those who hate him. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: स जामिभिर्यत समजाति मीळ्हे.अजामिभिर्वा पुरुहूत एवैः | अपां तोकस्य तनयस्य जेषे म... ||
1.100.e: When in his ways with kinsmen or with strangers he speedeth to the fight, invoked of many,  For gain of waters, and of sons and grandsons, may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: स वज्रभ्र्द दस्युहा भीम उग्रः सहस्रचेताः शतनीथर्भ्वा | चम्रीषो न शवसा पाञ्चजन्यो म... ||
1.100.e: Awful and fierce, fiend-slayer, thunder-wielder, with boundless knowledge, hymned by hundreds, mighty,  In strength like Soma, guard of the Five Peoples, may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: तस्य वज्रः करन्दति समत सवर्षा दिवो न तवेषो रवथःशिमीवान | तं सचन्ते सनयस्तं धनानि म... ||
1.100.e: Winning the light, hitherward roars his thunder like the terrific mighty voice of Heaven.  Rich gifts and treasures evermore attend him. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: यस्याजस्रं शवसा मानमुक्थं परिभुजद रोदसी विश्वतः सीम | स पारिषत करतुभिर्मन्दसानो म... ||
1.100.e: Whose home eternal through his strength surrounds him on every side, his laud, the earth and heaven,  May he, delighted with our service, save us. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.

1.100.d: न यस्य देवा देवता न मर्ता आपश्चन शवसो अन्तमापुः | स पररिक्वा तवक्षसा कष्मो दिवश्च म... ||
1.100.e: The limit of whose power not Gods by Godhead, nor mortal men have reached, nor yet the Waters.  Both Earth and Heaven in vigour he surpasseth. May Indra, girt by Maruts, he our succour.

1.100.d: रोहिच्छ्यावा सुमदंशुर्ललामीर्द्युक्षा राय रज्राश्वस्य | वर्षण्वन्तं बिभ्रती धूर्षु रथं मन्द्रा चिकेत नाहुषीषु विक्षु ||
1.100.e: The red and tawny mare, blaze-marked, high standing, celestial who, to bring Ṛjrāśva riches,  Drew at the pole the chariot yoked with stallions, joyous, among the hosts of men was noted.

1.100.d: एतत तयत त इन्द्र वर्ष्ण उक्थं वार्षागिरा अभि गर्णन्ति राधः | रज्राश्वः परष्टिभिरम्बरीषः सहदेवो भयमानः सुराधाः ||
1.100.e: The Vārṣāgiras unto thee, O Indra, the Mighty One, sing forth this laud to please thee,  Ṛjrāśva with his fellows, Ambarīṣa, Surādhas, Sahadeva, Bhayamāna.

1.100.d: दस्यूञ्छिम्यूंश्च पुरुहूत एवैर्हत्वा पर्थिव्यां शर्वा नि बर्हीत | सनत कषेत्रं सखिभिः शवित्न्येभिः सनत्सूर्यं सनदपः सुवज्रः ||
1.100.e: He, much invoked, hath slain Dasyus and Śimyus, after his wont, and laid them low with arrows.  The mighty Thunderer with his fair-complexioned friends won the land, the sunlight, and the waters.

1.100.d: विश्वाहेन्द्रो अधिवक्ता नो अस्त्वपरिह्व्र्ताः सनुयाम वाजम | तन नो ... ||
1.100.e: May Indra evermore be our protector, and unimperilled may we win the booty.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.101.d: पर मन्दिने पितुमदर्चता वचो यः कर्ष्णगर्भा निरहन्न्र्जिश्वना | अवस्यवो वर्षणं वज्रदक्षिणं मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ||
1.101.e: SING, with oblation, praise to him who maketh glad, who with Ṛjiśvan drove the dusky brood away.  Fain for help, him the strong whose right hand wields the bolt, him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.

1.101.d: यो वयंसं जाह्र्षाणेन मन्युना यः शम्बरं यो अहन पिप्रुमव्रतम | इन्द्रो यः शुष्णमशुषं नयाव्र्णं म. .. ||
1.101.e: Indra, who with triumphant wrath smote Vyaṁsa down, and Śambara, and Pipru the unrighteous one;  Who extirpated Śuṣṇa the insatiate,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.

1.101.d: यस्य दयावाप्र्थिवी पौंस्यं महद यस्य वरते वरुणो यस्य सूर्यः | यस्येन्द्रस्य सिन्धवः सश्चति वरतं म... ||
1.101.e: He whose great work of manly might is heaven and earth, and Varuṇa and Sūrya keep his holy law;  Indra, whose law the rivers follow as they flow,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.

1.101.d: यो अश्वानां यो गवां गोपतिर्वशी य आरितः कर्मणि कर्मणि सथिरः | वीळोश्चिदिन्द्रो यो असुन्वतो वधो म... ||
1.101.e: He who is Lord and Master of the steeds and kine, honoured—the firm and sure—at every holy act;  Stayer even of the strong who pours no offering out,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.

1.101.d: यो विश्वस्य जगतः पराणतस पतिर्यो बरह्मणे परथमो गा अविन्दत | इन्द्रो यो दस्यून्रधरानवातिरन म... ||
1.101.e: He who is Lord of all the world that moves and breathes, who for the Brahman first before all found the Cows;  Indra who cast the Dasyus down beneath his feet,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.

1.101.d: यः शूरेभिर्हव्यो यश्च भीरुभिर्यो धावद्भिर्हूयते यश्च जिग्युभिः | इन्द्रं यं विश्वा भुवनाभि सन्दधुर्म... ||
1.101.e: Whom cowards must invoke and valiant men of war, invoked by those who conquer and by those who flee;  Indra, to whom all beings turn their constant thought,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.

1.101.d: रुद्राणामेति परदिशा विचक्षणो रुद्रेभिर्योषा तनुते पर्थु जरयः | इन्द्रं मनीषा अभ्यर्चति शरुतं म... ||
1.101.e: Refulgent in the Rudras’ region he proceeds, and with the Rudras through the wide space speeds the Dame.  The hymn of praise extols Indra the far-renowned: him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.

1.101.d: यद वा मरुत्वः परमे सधस्थे यद वावमे वर्जने मादयासे | अत आ याह्यध्वरं नो अछा तवाया हविश्चक्र्मा सत्यराधः ||
1.101.e: O girt by Maruts, whether thou delight thee in loftiest gathering-place or lowly dwelling,  Come thence unto our rite, true boon-bestower: through love of thee have we prepared oblations.

1.101.d: तवायेन्द्र सोमं सुषुमा सुदक्ष तवाया हविश्चक्र्मा बरह्मवाहः | अधा नियुत्वः सगणो मरुद्भिरस्मिन यज्ञे बर्हिषिमादयस्व ||
1.101.e: We, fain for thee, strong Indra, have pressed Soma, and, O thou sought with prayer, have made oblations.  Now at this sacrifice, with all thy Maruts, on sacred grass, O team-borne God, rejoice thee.

1.101.d: मादयस्व हरिभिर्ये त इन्द्र वि षयस्व शिप्रे वि सर्जस्व धेने | आ तवा सुशिप्र हरयो वहन्तूशन हव्यानि परति नो जुषस्व ||
1.101.e: Rejoice thee with thine own Bay Steeds, O Indra, unclose thy jaws and let thy lips be open.  Thou with the fair cheek, let thy Bay Steeds bring thee: gracious to us, he pleased with our oblation.

1.101.d: मरुत्स्तोत्रस्य वर्जनस्य गोपा वयमिन्द्रेण सनुयाम वाजम | तन नो ... ||
1.101.e: Guards of the camp whose praisers are the Maruts, may we through Indra, get ourselves the booty.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.102.d: इमां ते धियं पर भरे महो महीमस्य सतोत्रे धिषणायत त आनजे | तमुत्सवे च परसवे च सासहिमिन्द्रं देवासः शवसामदन्ननु ||
1.102.e: To thee the Mighty One I bring this mighty hymn, for thy desire hath been gratified by my laud.  In Indra, yea in him victorious through his strength, the Gods have joyed at feast and when the Soma flowed.

1.102.d: अस्य शरवो नद्यः सप्त बिभ्रति दयावाक्षामा पर्थिवी दर्शतं वपुः | अस्मे सूर्याचन्द्रमसाभिचक्षे शरद्धे कमिन्द्र चरतो वितर्तुरम ||
1.102.e: The Seven Rivers bear his glory far and wide, and heaven and sky and earth display his comely form.  The Sun and Moon in change alternate run their course, that we, O Indra, may behold and may have faith.

1.102.d: तं समा रथं मघवन्न्प्राव सातये जैत्रं यं ते अनुमदाम संगमे | आजा न इन्द्र मनसा पुरुष्टुत तवायद्भ्यो मघवञ्छर्म यछ नः ||
1.102.e: Maghavan, grant us that same car to bring us spoil, thy conquering car in which we joy in shock of fight.  Thou, Indra, whom our hearts praise highly in the war, grant shelter, Maghavan, to us who love thee well.

1.102.d: वयं जयेम तवया युजा वर्तमस्माकमंशमुदवा भरे-भरे | अस्मभ्यमिन्द्र वरिवः सुगं कर्धि पर शत्रूणांमघवन वर्ष्ण्या रुज ||
1.102.e: Encourage thou our side in every fight: may we, with thee for our ally, conquer the foeman's host.  Indra, bestow on us joy and felicity break down, O Maghavan, the vigour of our foes.

1.102.d: नाना हि तवा हवमाना जना इमे धनानां धर्तरवसाविपन्यवः | अस्माकं समा रथमा तिष्ठ सातये जैत्रंहीन्द्र निभ्र्तं मनस्तव ||
1.102.e: For here in divers ways these men invoking thee, holder of treasures, sing hymns to win thine aid.  Ascend the car that thou mayest bring spoil to us, for, Indra, thy fixt winneth the victory.

1.102.d: गोजिता बाहू अमितक्रतुः सिमः कर्मन कर्मञ्छतमूतिः खजंकरः | अकल्प इन्द्रः परतिमानमोजसाथा जना विह्वयन्ते सिषासवः ||
1.102.e: His arms win kine, his power is boundless in each act best, with a hundred helps, waker of battle's din  Is Indra: none may rival him in mighty strength. Hence, eager for the spoil the people call on him.

1.102.d: उत ते शतान मघवन्नुच्च भूयस उत सहस्राद रिरिचे कर्ष्टिषु शरवः | अमात्रं तवा धिषणा तित्विषे मह्यधा वर्त्राणि जिघ्नसे पुरन्दर ||
1.102.e: Thy glory, Maghavan, exceeds a hundred yea, more than a hundred, than a thousand mid the folk,  The great bowl hath inspirited thee boundlessly: so mayst thou slay the Vṛtras, breaker-down of forts!

1.102.d: तरिविष्टिधातु परतिमानमोजसस्तिस्रो भूमीर्न्र्पते तरीणि रोचना | अतीदं विश्वं भुवनं ववक्षिथाशत्रुरिन्द्रजनुषा सनादसि ||
1.102.e: Of thy great might there is a three counterpart, the three earths, Lord men and the three realms of light.  Above this whole world, Indra, thou hast waxen great: without a foe art thou, nature, from of old.

1.102.d: तवां देवेषु परथमं हवामहे तवं बभूथ पर्तनासु सासहिः | सेमं नः कारुमुपमन्युमुद्भिदमिन्द्रः कर्णोतु परसवे रथं पुरः ||
1.102.e: We invocate thee first among the Deities: thou hast become a mighty Conquer in fight.  May Indra fill with spirit this our singer's heart, and make our car impetuous, foremost in attack.

1.102.d: तवं जिगेथ न धना रुरोधिथार्भेष्वाजा मघवन महत्सु च | तवामुग्रमवसे सं शिशीमस्यथा न इन्द्र हवनेषु चोदय ||
1.102.e: Thou hast prevailed, and hast not kept the booty back, in trifling battles in those of great account.  We make thee keen, the Mighty One, succour us: inspire us, Maghavan, when we defy the foe.
May Indra evermore be our Protector, and unimperilled may we win the booty.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.103.d: तत त इन्द्रियं परमं पराचैरधारयन्त कवयः पुरेदम | कषमेदमन्यद दिव्यन्यदस्य समी पर्च्यते समनेव केतुः ||
1.103.e: THAT highest Indra-power of thine is distant: that which is here sages possessed aforetime.  This one is on the earth, in heaven the other, and both unite as flag with flag in battle.

1.103.d: स धारयत पर्थिवीं पप्रथच्च वज्रेण हत्वा निरपः ससर्ज | अहन्नहिमभिनद रौहिणं वयहन वयंसं मघवा शचीभिः ||
1.103.e: He spread the wide earth out and firmly fixed it, smote with his thunderbolt and loosed the waters.  Maghavan with his puissance struck down Ahi, rent Rauhiṇa to death and slaughtered Vyaṁsa.

1.103.d: स जातूभर्मा शरद्दधान ओजः पुरो विभिन्दन्नचरद विदासीः | विद्वान वज्रिन दस्यवे हेतिमस्यार्यं सहो वर्धया दयुम्नमिन्द्र ||
1.103.e: Armed with his bolt and trusting in his prowess he wandered shattering the forts of Dāsas.  Cast thy dart, knowing, Thunderer, at the Dasyu; increase the Ārya's might and glory, Indra.

1.103.d: तदूचुषे मानुषेमा युगानि कीर्तेन्यं मघवा नाम बिभ्रत | उपप्रयन दस्युहत्याय वज्री यद ध सूनुः शरवसे नाम दधे ||
1.103.e: For him who thus hath taught these human races, Maghavan, bearing a fame-worthy title,  Thunderer, drawing nigh to slay the Dasyus, hath given himself the name of Son for glory.

1.103.d: तदस्येदं पश्यता भूरि पुष्टं शरदिन्द्रस्य धत्तन वीर्याय | स गा अविन्दत सो अविन्ददश्वान स ओषधीः सोपः स वनानि ||
1.103.e: See this abundant wealth that he possesses, and put your trust in Indra's hero vigour.  He found the cattle, and he found the horses, he found the plants, the forests and the waters.

1.103.d: भुरिकर्मणे वर्षभाय वर्ष्णे सत्यशुष्माय सुनवाम सोमम | य आद्र्त्या परिपन्थीव शूरो.अयज्वनो विभजन्नेति वेदः ||
1.103.e: To him the truly strong, whose deeds are many, to him the strong Bull let us pour the Soma.  The Hero, watching like a thief in ambush, goes parting the possessions of the godless.

1.103.d: तदिन्द्र परेव वीर्यं चकर्थ यत ससन्तं वज्रेणाबोधयो.अहिम | अनु तवा पत्नीर्ह्र्षितं वयश्च विश्वे देवासो अमदन्ननु तवा ||
1.103.e: Well didst thou do that hero deed, O Indra, in waking with thy bolt the slumbering Ahi.  in thee, delighted, Dames divine rejoiced them, the flying Maruts and all Gods were joyful.

1.103.d: शुष्णं पिप्रुं कुयवं वर्त्रमिन्द्र यदावधीर्वि पुरःशम्बरस्य | तन नो ... ||
1.103.e: As thou hast smitten Śuṣṇa, Pipru, Vṛtra and Kuyava, and Śambara's forts  ,  O Indra.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.104.d: योनिष ट इन्द्र निषदे अकारि तमा नि षीद सवानो नार्वा | विमुच्य वयो.अवसायाश्वान दोषा वस्तोर्वहीयसः परपित्वे ||
1.104.e: THE altar hath been made for thee to rest on: come like a panting courser and be seated.  Loosen thy flying Steeds, set free thy Horses who bear thee swiftly nigh at eve and morning.

1.104.d: ओ तये नर इन्द्रमूतये गुर्नू चित तान सद्यो अध्वनो जगम्यात | देवासो मन्युं दासस्य शचम्नन ते न आ वक्षन सुविताय वर्णम ||
1.104.e: These men have come to Indra for assistance: shall he not quickly come upon these pathways?  May the Gods quell the fury of the Dāsa, and may they lead our folk to happy fortune.

1.104.d: अव तमन भरते केतवेदा अव तमना भरते फेनमुदन | कषीरेण सनातः कुयवस्य योषे हते ते सयातां परवणे शिफायाः ||
1.104.e: He who hath only wish as his possession casts on himself, casts foam amid the waters.  Both wives of Kuyava in milk have bathed them: may they be drowned within the depth of Śiphā.

1.104.d: युयोप नाभिरुपरस्यायोः पर पूर्वाभिस्तिरते राष्टि शूरः | अञ्जसी कुलिशी वीरपत्नी पयो हिन्वाना उदभिर्भरन्ते ||
1.104.e: This hath his kinship checked who lives beside us: with ancient streams forth speeds and rules the Hero,  Añjasī, Kuliśī, and Virapatnī, delighting him, bear milk upon their waters.

1.104.d: परति यत सया नीथादर्शि दस्योरोको नाछा सदनं जानती गात | अध समा नो मघवञ्चर्क्र्तादिन मा नो मघेव निष्षपी परा दाः ||
1.104.e: Soon as this Dasyu's traces were discovered, as she who knows her home, he sought the dwelling.  Now think thou of us, Maghavan, nor cast us away as doth a profligate his treasure.

1.104.d: स तवं न इन्द्र सूर्ये सो अप्स्वनागास्त्व आ भज जीवशंसे | मान्तरां भुजमा रीरिषो नः शरद्धितं ते महत इन्द्रियाय ||
1.104.e: Indra, as such, give us a share of sunlight, of waters, sinlessness, and reputation.  Do thou no harm to our yet unborn offspring: our trust is in thy mighty Indra-power.

1.104.d: अधा मन्ये शरत ते अस्मा अधायि वर्षा चोदस्व महते धनाय | मा नो अक्र्ते पुरुहूत योनाविन्द्र कषुध्यद्भ्यो वय आसुतिं दाः ||
1.104.e: Now we, I think, in thee as such have trusted: lead us on, Mighty One, to ample riches.  In no unready house give us, O Indra invoked of many, food and drink when hungry.

1.104.d: मा नो वधीरिन्द्र मा परा दा मा नः परिया भोजनानि पर मोषीः | आण्डा मा नो मघवञ्छक्र निर्भेन मा नः पात्रा भेत सहजानुषाणि ||
1.104.e: Slay us not, Indra; do not thou forsake us: steal not away the joys which we delight in.  Rend not our unborn brood, strong Lord of Bounty! our vessels with the life that is within them.

1.104.d: अर्वां एहि सोमकामं तवाहुरयं सुतस्तस्य पिबा मदाय | उरुव्यचा जथर आ वर्षस्व पितेव नः शर्णुहि हूयमानः ||
1.104.e: Come to us; they have called thee Soma-lover: here is the pressed juice. Drink thereof for rapture.  Widely-capacious, pour it down within thee, and, invocated, hear us like a Father.

1.105.d: चन्द्रमा अप्स्वन्तरा सुपर्णो धावते दिवि | न वो हिरण्यनेमयः पदं विन्दन्ति विद्युतो वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ||
1.105.e: WITHIN the waters runs the Moon, he with the beauteous wings in heaven.  Ye lightnings with your golden wheels, men find not your abiding-place. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: अर्थमिद वा उ अर्थिन आ जाया युवते पतिम | तुञ्जाते वर्ष्ण्यं पयः परिदाय रसं दुहे वित्तम... ||
1.105.e: Surely men crave and gain their wish. Close to her husband clings the wife.  And, in embraces intertwined, both give and take the bliss of love. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: मो षु देव अदः सवरव पादि दिवस परि | मा सोम्यस्य शम्भुवः शूने भूम कदा चन वित्तम... ||
1.105.e: O never may that light, ye Gods, fall from its station in the sky.  Ne’er fail us one like Soma sweet, the spring of our felicity. Mark this my woe  ,  ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: यज्ञं पर्छाम्यवमं स तद दूतो वि वोचति | कव रतं पूर्व्यं गतं कस्तद बिभर्ति नूतनो वि... ||
1.105.e: I ask the last of sacrifice. As envoy he shall tell it forth.  Where is the ancient law divine? Who is its new diffuser now? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: अमी ये देवा सथन तरिष्वा रोचने दिवः | कद व रतं कदन्र्तं कव परत्ना व आहुतिर्वि... ||
1.105.e: Ye Gods who yonder have your home in the three lucid realms of heaven,  What count ye truth and what untruth? Where is mine ancient call on you? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: कद व रतस्य धर्णसि कद वरुणस्य चक्षणम | कदर्यम्णो महस पथाति करामेम दूढ्यो वि... ||
1.105.e: What is your firm support of Law? What Varuṇa's observant eye?  How may we pass the wicked on the path of mighty Aryaman? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: अहम सो अस्मि यः पुरा सुते वदामि कानि चित | तं मा वयन्त्याध्यो वर्को न तर्ष्णजं मर्गं वि... ||
1.105.e: I am the man who sang of old full many a laud when Soma flowed.  Yet torturing cares consume me as the wolf assails the thirsty deer. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: सं मा तपन्त्यभितः सपत्नीरिव पर्शवः | मूषो न शिश्ना वयदन्ति माध्य सतोतारं ते शतक्रतो वि... ||
1.105.e: Like rival wives on every side enclosing ribs oppress me sore.  O Śatakratu, biting cares devour me, singer of thy praise, as rats devour the weaver's threads. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: अमी ये सप्त रश्मयस्तत्रा मे नाभिरातता | तरितस्तद वेदाप्त्यः स जामित्वाय रेभति वि... ||
1.105.e: Where those seven rays are shining, thence my home and family extend.  This Tṛta Āptya knoweth well, and speaketh out for brotherhood. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: अमी ये पञ्चोक्षणो मध्ये तस्थुर्महो दिवः | देवत्रा नु परवाच्यं सध्रीचीना नि वाव्र्तुर्वि... ||
1.105.e: May those five Bulls which stand on high full in the midst of mighty heaven,  Having together swiftly borne my praises to the Gods, return. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: सुपर्णा एत आसते मध्य आरोधने दिवः | ते सेधन्ति पथो वर्कं तरन्तं यह्वतीरपो वि... ||
1.105.e: High in the mid ascent of heaven those Birds of beauteous pinion sit.  Back from his path they drive the wolf as he would cross the restless floods. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: नव्यं तदुक्थ्यं हितं देवासः सुप्रवाचनम | रतमर्षन्ति सिन्धवः सत्यं तातान सूर्यो वि... ||
1.105.e: Firm is this new-wrought hymn of praise, and meet to be told forth, O Gods.  The flowing of the floods is Law, Truth is the Sun's extended light. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: अग्ने तव तयदुक्थ्यं देवेष्वस्त्याप्यम | स नः सत्तो मनुष्वदा देवान यक्षि विदुष्टरो वि... ||
1.105.e: Worthy of laud, O Agni, is that kinship which thou hast with Gods.  Here seat thee like a man: most wise, bring thou the Gods for sacrifice. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: सत्तो होता मनुष्वदा देवानछा विदुष्टरः | अग्निर्हव्या सुषूदति देवो देवेषु मेधिरो वि... ||
1.105.e: Here seated, man-like as a priest shall wisest Agni to the Gods  Speed onward our oblations, God among the Gods, intelligent. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: बरह्मा कर्णोति वरुणो गातुविदं तमीमहे | वयूर्णोति हर्दा मतिं नव्यो जायतां रतं वि... ||
1.105.e: Varuṇa makes the holy prayer. To him who finds the path we pray.  He in the heart reveals his thought. Let sacred worship rise anew. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: असौ यः पन्था आदित्यो दिवि परवाच्यं कर्तः | न स देवा अतिक्रमे तं मर्तासो न पश्यथ वि... ||
1.105.e: That pathway of the Sun in heaven, made to be highly glorified,  Is not to be transgressed, O Gods. O mortals, ye behold it not. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: तरितः कूपे.अवहितो देवान हवत ऊतये | तच्छुश्राव बर्हस्पतिः कर्ण्वन्नंहूरणादुरु वि... ||
1.105.e: Tṛta, when buried in the well, calls on the Gods to succour him.  That call of his Bṛhaspati heard and released him from distress. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: अरुणो मा सक्र्द वर्कः पथा यन्तं ददर्श हि | उज्जिहीते निचाय्या तष्टेव पर्ष्ट्यामयी वि... ||
1.105.e: A ruddy wolf beheld me once, as I was faring on my path.  He, like a carpenter whose back is aching crouched and slunk away. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.

1.105.d: एनाङगूषेण वयमिन्द्रवन्तो.अभि षयाम वर्जने सर्ववीराः | तन नो ... ||
1.105.e: Through this our song may we, allied with Indra, with all our heroes conquer in the battle.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.106.d: इन्द्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमूतये मारुतं शर्धो अदितिंहवामहे | रथं न दुर्गाद वसवः सुदानवो विश्वस्मान नोंहसो निष पिपर्तन ||
1.106.e: CALL we for aid on Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni and the Marut host and Aditi.  Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.

1.106.d: त आदित्या आ गता सर्वतातये भूत देवा वर्त्रतूर्येषु शम्भुवः | रथं ... ||
1.106.e: Come ye Ādityas for our full prosperity, in conquests of the foe, ye Gods, bring joy to us.  Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.

1.106.d: अवन्तु नः पितरः सुप्रवाचना उत देवी देवपुत्रे रताव्र्धा | रथं ... ||
1.106.e: May the most glorious Fathers aid us, and the two Goddesses, Mothers of the Gods, who strengthen Law.  Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.

1.106.d: नराशंसं वाजिनं वाजयन्निह कषयद्वीरं पूषणं सुम्नैरीमहे | रथं ... ||
1.106.e: To mighty Narāśaṁsa, strengthening his might, to Pūṣan, ruler over men, we pray with hymns.  Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.

1.106.d: बर्हस्पते सदमिन नः सुगं कर्धि शं योर्यत ते मनुर्हितं तदीमहे | रथं ... ||
1.106.e: Bṛhaspati, make us evermore an easy path: we crave what boon thou hast for men in rest and stir.  Like as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.

1.106.d: इन्द्रं कुत्सो वर्त्रहणं शचीपतिं काटे निबाळ्ह रषिरह्वदूतये | रथं ... ||
1.106.e: Sunk in the pit the Ṛṣi Kutsa called, to aid, Indra the Vṛtra-slayer, Lord of power and might.  Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.

1.106.d: देवैर्नो देव्यदितिर्नि पातु देवस्त्राता तरायतामप्रयुछन | तन नो ... ||
1.106.e: May Aditi the Goddess guard us with the Gods: may the protecting God keep us with ceaseless care.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.107.d: यज्ञो देवानां परत्येति सुम्नमादित्यासो भवता मर्ळयन्तः | आ वो.अर्वाची सुमतिर्वव्र्त्यादंहोश्चिद या वरिवोवित्तरासत ||
1.107.e: THE sacrifice obtains the Gods’ acceptance: be graciously inclined to us, Ādityas.  Hitherward let your favour be directed, and be our best deliverer from trouble.

1.107.d: उप नो देवा अवसा गमन्त्वङगिरसां सामभिः सतूयमानाः | इन्द्र इन्द्रियैर्मरुतो मरुद्भिरादित्यैर्नो अदितिः शर्म यंसत ||
1.107.e: By praise-songs of Aṅgirases exalted, may the Gods come to us with their protection.  May Indra with his powers, Maruts with Maruts, Aditi with Ādityas grant us shelter.

1.107.d: तन न इन्द्रस्तद वरुणस्तदग्निस्तदर्यमा तत सविताचनो धात | तन नो ... ||
1.107.e: This laud of ours may Varuṇa and Indra, Aryaman Agni, Savitar find pleasant.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.108.d: य इन्द्राग्नी चित्रतमो रथो वामभि विश्वानि भुवनानि चष्टे | तेना यातं सरथं तस्थिवांसाथा सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ||
1.108.e: ON that most wondrous car of yours, O Indra and Agni, which looks round on all things living,  Take ye your stand and come to us together, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.

1.108.d: यावदिदं भुवनं विश्वमस्त्युरुव्यचा वरिमता गभीरम | तावानयं पातवे सोमो अस्त्वरमिन्द्राग्नी मनसे युवभ्याम ||
1.108.e: As vast as all this world is in its compass, deep as it is, with its far-stretching surface,  So let this Soma be, Indra and Agni, made for your drinking till your soul be sated.

1.108.d: चक्राथे हि सध्र्यं नाम भद्रं सध्रीचीना वर्त्रहणाुत सथः | ताविन्द्राग्नी सध्र्यञ्चा निषद्या वर्ष्णः सोमस्य वर्षणा वर्षेथाम ||
1.108.e: For ye have won a blessed name together: yea, with one aim ye strove, O Vṛtra-slayers.  So Indra-Agni, seated here together, pour in, ye Mighty Ones, the mighty Soma.

1.108.d: समिद्धेष्वग्निष्वानजाना यतस्रुचा बर्हिरु तिस्तिराणा | तीव्रैः सोमैः परिषिक्तेभिरर्वागेन्द्राग्नी सौमनसाय यातम ||
1.108.e: Both stand adorned, when fires are duly kindled, spreading the sacred grass, with lifted ladles.  Drawn by strong Soma juice poured forth around us, come, Indra-Agni, and display your favour.

1.108.d: यानीन्द्राग्नी चक्रथुर्वीर्याणि यानि रूपाण्युत वर्ष्ण्यानि | या वां परत्नानि सख्या शिवानि तेभिः सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ||
1.108.e: The brave deeds ye have done, Indra and Agni, the forms ye have displayed and mighty exploits,  The ancient and auspicious bonds of friendship,—for sake of these drink of the flowing Soma.

1.108.d: यदब्रवं परथमं वां वर्णानो.अयं सोमो असुरैर्नो विहव्यः | तां सत्यां शरद्धामभ्या हि यातमथा सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ||
1.108.e: As first I said when choosing you, in battle we must contend with Asuras for this Soma.  So came ye unto this my true conviction, and drank libations of the flowing Soma.

1.108.d: यदिन्द्राग्नी मदथः सवे दुरोणे यद बरह्मणि राजनि वायजत्रा | अतः परि वर्षणावा हि यातमथा सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ||
1.108.e: If in your dwelling, or with prince or Brahman, ye, Indra-Agni, Holy Ones, rejoice you,  Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libation of the flowing Soma.

1.108.d: यदिन्द्राग्नी यदुषु तुर्वशेषु यद दरुह्युष्वनुषु पूरुषु सथः | अतः ... ||
1.108.e: If with, the Yadus, Turvaśas, ye sojourn, with Druhyus, Anus, Pūrus, Indra-Agni!  Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.

1.108.d: यदिन्द्राग्नी अवमस्यां पर्थिव्यां मध्यमस्यां परमस्यामुत सथः | अतः ... ||
1.108.e: Whether, O Indra-Agni, ye be dwelling in lowest earth, in central, or in highest.  Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.

1.108.d: यदिन्द्राग्नी परमस्यां पर्थिव्यां मध्यमस्यामवमस्यामुत सथः | अतः ... ||
1.108.e: Whether, O Indra-Agni, ye be dwelling in highest earth, in central, or in lowest,  Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.

1.108.d: यदिन्द्राग्नी दिवि षठो यत पर्थिव्यां यत पर्वतेष्वोषधीष्वप्सु | अतः ... ||
1.108.e: Whether ye be in heaven, O Indra-Agni, on earth, on mountains, in the herbs, or waters,  Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.

1.108.d: यदिन्द्राग्नी उदिता सूर्यस्य मध्ये दिवः सवधया मादयेथे | अतः ... ||
1.108.e: If, when the Sun to the mid-heaven hath mounted, ye take delight in food, O Indra-Agni,  Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.

1.108.d: एवेन्द्राग्नी पपिवांसा सुतस्य विश्वास्मभ्यं सं जयतन्धनानि | तन नो ... ||
1.108.e: Thus having drunk your fill of our libation, win us all kinds of wealth, Indra and Agni.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.109.d: वि हयख्यं मनसा वस्य इछन्निन्द्राग्नी जञास उत वा सजातान | नान्या युवत परमतिरस्ति मह्यं स वां धियं वाजयन्तीमतक्षम ||
1.109.e: LONGING for weal I looked around, in spirit, for kinsmen, Indra-Agni, or for brothers.  No providence but yours alone is with me so have I wrought for you this hymn for succour.

1.109.d: अश्रवं हि भूरिदावत्तरा वां विजामातुरुत वा घा सयालात | अथा सोमस्य परयती युवभ्यामिन्द्राग्नी सतोमं जनयामि नव्यम ||
1.109.e: For I have heard that ye give wealth more freely than worthless son-in-law or spouse's brother.  So offering to you this draught of Soma, I make you this new hymn, Indra and Agni,

1.109.d: मा छेद्म रश्मीन्रिति नाधमानाः पितॄणां शक्तीरनुयछमानाः | इन्द्राग्निभ्यां कं वर्षणो मदन्ति ता हयद्री धिषणाया उपस्थे ||
1.109.e: Let us not break the cords: with this petition we strive to gain the powers of our forefathers.  For Indra-Agni the strong drops are joyful, for here in the bowl's lap are both the press-stones.

1.109.d: युवाभ्यां देवी धिषणा मदायेन्द्राग्नी सोममुशती सुनोति | तावश्विना भद्रहस्ता सुपाणी आ धावतं मधुना पर्ङकतमप्सु ||
1.109.e: For you the bowl divine, Indra and Agni, presses the Soma gladly to delight you.  With hands auspicious and fair arms, ye Aśvins, haste, sprinkle it with sweetness in the waters.

1.109.d: युवामिन्द्राग्नी वसुनो विभागे तवस्तमा शुश्रव वर्त्रहत्ये | तावासद्या बर्हिषि यज्ञे अस्मिन पर चर्षणी मादयेथां सुतस्य ||
1.109.e: You, I have heard, were mightiest, Indra-Agni, when Vṛtra fell and when the spoil was parted.  Sit at this sacrifice, ye ever active, on the strewn grass, and with the juice delight you.

1.109.d: पर चर्षणिभ्यः पर्तनाहवेषु पर पर्थिव्या रिरिचाथे दिवश्च | पर सिन्धुभ्यः पर गिरिभ्यो महित्वा परेन्द्राग्नी विश्वा भुवनात्यन्या ||
1.109.e: Surpassing all men where they shout for battle, ye Twain exceed the earth and heaven in greatness.  Greater are ye than rivers and than mountains, O Indra-Agni, and all things beside them.

1.109.d: आ भरतं शिक्षतं वज्रबाहू अस्मानिन्द्राग्नी अवतं शचीभिः | इमे नु ते रश्मयः सूर्यस्य येभिः सपित्वं पितरो न आसन ||
1.109.e: Bring wealth and give it, ye whose arms wield thunder: Indra and Agni, with your powers protect us.  Now of a truth these be the very sunbeams wherewith our fathers were of old united.

1.109.d: पुरन्दरा शिक्षतं वज्रहस्तास्मानिन्द्राग्नी अवतं भरेषु | तन नो ... ||
1.109.e: Give, ye who shatter forts, whose hands wield thunder: Indra and Agni, save us in our battles.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.110.d: ततं मे अपस्तदु तायते पुनः सवादिष्ठा धीतिरुचथाय शस्यते | अयं समुद्र इह विश्वदेव्यः सवाहाक्र्तस्य समु तर्प्णुत रभवः ||
1.110.e: THE holy work I wrought before is wrought again: my sweetest hymn is sung to celebrate your praise.  Here, O ye Ṛbhus, is this sea for all the Gods: sate you with Soma offered with the hallowing word.

1.110.d: आभोगयं पर यदिछन्त ऐतनापाकाः पराञ्चो मम के चिदापयः | सौधन्वनासश्चरितस्य भूमनागछत सवितुर्दाशुषो गर्हम ||
1.110.e: When, seeking your enjoyment onward from afar, ye, certain of my kinsmen, wandered on your way,  Sons of Sudhanvan, after your long journeying, ye came unto the home of liberal Savitar.

1.110.d: तत सविता वो.अम्र्तत्वामासुवदगोह्यं यच्छ्रवयन्त ऐतन | तयं चिच्चमसमसुरस्य भक्षणमेकं सन्तमक्र्णुता चतुर्वयम ||
1.110.e: Savitar therefore gave you immortality, because ye came proclaiming him whom naught can hide;  And this the drinking-chalice of the Asura, which till that time was one, ye made to be fourfold.

1.110.d: विष्ट्वी शमी तरणित्वेन वाघतो मर्तासः सन्तो अम्र्तत्वमानशुः | सौधन्वना रभवः सूरचक्षसः संवत्सरे समप्र्च्यन्त धीतिभिः ||
1.110.e: When they had served with zeal at sacrifice as priests, they, mortal as they were, gained immortality.  The Ṛbhus, children of Sudhanvan, bright as suns, were in a year's course made associate with prayers.

1.110.d: कषेत्रमिव वि ममुस्तेजनेनमेकं पात्रं रभवो जेहमानम | उपस्तुता उपमं नाधमाना अमर्त्येषु शरव इछमानाः ||
1.110.e: The Ṛbhus, with a rod measured, as ’twere a field, the single sacrificial chalice. wide of mouth,  Lauded of all who saw, praying for what is best, desiring glorious fame among Immortal Gods.

1.110.d: आ मनीषामन्तरिक्षस्य नर्भ्यः सरुचेव घर्तं जुहवाम विद्मना | तरणित्वा ये पितुरस्य सश्चिर रभवो वाजमरुहन दिवो रजः ||
1.110.e: As oil in ladles, we through knowledge will present unto the Heroes of the firmament our hymn,—  The Ṛbhus who came near with this great Father's speed, and rose to heaven's high sphere to eat the strengthening food.

1.110.d: रभुर्न इन्द्रः शवसा नवीयान रभुर्वाजेभिर्वसुभिर्वसुर्ददिः | युष्माकं देवा अवसाहनि परिये.अभि तिष्ठेमप्र्त्सुतीरसुन्वताम ||
1.110.e: Ṛbhu to us is Indra freshest in his might, Ṛbhu with powers and wealth is giver of rich gifts.  Gods, through your favour may we on the happy day quell the attacks of those who pour no offerings forth.

1.110.d: निश्चर्मण रभवो गामपिंशत सं वत्सेनास्र्जता मातरं पुनः | सौधन्वनासः सवपस्यया नरो जिव्री युवाना पितराक्र्णोतन ||
1.110.e: Out of a skin, O Ṛbhus, once ye formed a cow, and brought the mother close unto her calf again.  Sons of Sudhanvan, Heroes, with surpassing skill ye made your aged Parents youthful as before.

1.110.d: वाजेभिर्नो वाजसातावविड्ढ्य रभुमानिन्द्र चित्रमा दर्षि राधः | तन नो ... ||
1.110.e: Help us with strength where spoil is won, O Indra: joined with the Ṛbhus give us varied bounty.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.111.d: तक्षन रथं सुव्र्तं विदम्नापसस्तक्षन हरी इन्द्रवाहा वर्षण्वसू | तक्षन पित्र्भ्यां रभवो युवद वयस्तक्षन्वत्साय मातरं सचाभुवम ||
1.111.e: WORKING with skill they wrought the lightly rolling car: they wrought the Bays who bear Indra and bring great gifts.  The Ṛbhus for their Parents made life young again; and fashioned for the calf a mother by its side.

1.111.d: आ नो यज्ञाय तक्षत रभुमद वयः करत्वे दक्षाय सुप्रजावतीमिषम | यथा कषयाम सर्ववीरया विशा तन नःशर्धाय धासथा सविन्द्रियम ||
1.111.e: For sacrifice make for us active vital power for skill and wisdom food with noble progeny.  Grant to our company this power most excellent, that with a family all-heroic we may dwell.

1.111.d: आ तक्षत सातिमस्मभ्यं रभवः सातिं रथाय सातिमर्वते नरः | सातिं नो जैत्रीं सं महेत विश्वहा जामिमजामिं पर्तनासु सक्षणिम ||
1.111.e: Do ye, O Ṛbhus, make prosperity for us, prosperity for car, ye Heroes, and for steed.  Grant us prosperity victorious evermore,  conquering foes in battle, strangers or akin.

1.111.d: रभुक्षणमिन्द्रमा हुव ऊतय रभून वाजान मरुतः सोमपीतये | उभा मित्रावरुणा नूनमश्विना ते नो हिन्वन्तु सातये धिये जिषे ||
1.111.e: Indra, the Ṛbhus' Lord, I invocate for aid, the Ṛbhus, Vājas, Maruts to the Soma draught.  Varuṇa, Mitra, both, yea, and the Aśvins Twain: let them speed us to wealth, wisdom, and victory.

1.111.d: रभुर्भराय सं शिशातु सातिं समर्यजिद वाजो अस्मानविष्टु | तन नो ... ||
1.111.e: May Ṛbhu send prosperity for battle, may Vāja conquering in the fight protect us.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.112.d: ईळे दयावाप्र्थिवी पूर्वचित्तये.अग्निं घर्मं सुरुचं यामन्निष्टये | याभिर्भरे कारमंशाय जिन्वथस्ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम ||
1.112.e: To give first thought to them, I worship Heaven and Earth, and Agni, fair bright glow, to hasten their approach.  Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith in fight ye speed the war-cry to the spoil.

1.112.d: युवोर्दानाय सुभरा असश्चतो रथमा तस्थुर्वचसं न मन्तवे | याभिर्धियो.अवथःकर्मन्निष्टये ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Ample, unfailing, they have mounted as it were an eloquent car that ye may think of us and give.  Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith ye help our thoughts to further holy acts.

1.112.d: युवं तासां दिव्यस्य परशासने विशां कषयथो अम्र्तस्यमज्मना | याभिर्धेनुमस्वं पिन्वथो नरा ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Ye by the might which heavenly nectar giveth you are in supreme dominion Lords of all these folk.  Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith ye, Heroes, made the barren cow give milk.

1.112.d: याभिः परिज्मा तनयस्य मज्मना दविमाता तूर्षु तरणिर्विभूषति | याभिस्त्रिमन्तुरभवद विचक्षणस्ताभिर.. . ||
1.112.e: The aids wherewith the Wanderer through his offspring's might, or the Two-Mothered Son shows swiftest mid the swift;  Wherewith the sapient one acquired his triple lore,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभी रेभं निव्र्तं सितमद्भ्य उद वन्दनमैरयतं सवर्द्र्शे | याभिः कण्वं पर सिषासन्तमावतं ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith ye raised from waters, prisoned and fast bound, Rebha, and Vandana to look upon the light;  Wherewith ye succoured Kaṇva as he strove to win,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिरन्तकं जसमानमारणे भुज्यं याभिरव्यथिभिर्जिजिन्वथुः | याभिः कर्कन्धुं वय्यं च जिन्वथस्ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith ye rescued Antaka when languishing deep in the pit, and Bhujyu with unfailing help.  And comforted Karkandhu, Vayya, in their woe,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिः शुचन्तिं धनसां सुषंसदं तप्तं घर्ममोम्यावन्तमत्रये | याभिः पर्ष्निगुं पुरुकुत्समावतं ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith ye gave Śucanti wealth and happy home, and made the fiery pit friendly for Atri's sake;  Wherewith ye guarded Purukutsa, Pṛśnigu,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvin;, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिः शचीभिर्व्र्षणा पराव्र्जं परान्धं शरोणं चक्षस एतवे कर्थः | याभिर्वर्तिकां गरसिताममुञ्चतन्ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Mighty Ones, with what powers ye gave Parāvṛj aid what time ye made the blind and lame to see and walk;  Wherewith ye set at liberty the swallowed quail,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिः सिन्धुं मधुमन्तमसश्चतं वसिष्ठं याभिरजरावजिन्वतम | याभिः कुत्सं शरुतर्यं नर्यमावतं ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith ye quickened the most sweet exhaustless flood, and comforted Vasiṣṭha, ye who ne’er decay;  And to Śrutarya, Kutsa, Narya gave your help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिर्विश्पलां धनसामथर्व्यं सहस्रमीळ्ह आजावजिन्वतम | याभिर्वशमश्व्यं परेणिमावतं ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith ye helped, in battle of a thousand spoils, Viśpalā seeking booty, powerless to move.  Wherewith ye guarded friendly Vaśa, Aśva's son,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिः सुदानू औशिजाय वणिजे दीर्घश्रवसे मधु कोशोक्षरत | कक्षीवन्तं सतोतारं याभिरावतं ताभिर. .. ||
1.112.e: Whereby the cloud, ye Bounteous Givers, shed sweet rain for Dīrghaśravas, for the merchant Auśija,  Wherewith ye helped Kakṣīvān, singer of your praise,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभी रसां कषोदसोद्नः पिपिन्वथुरनश्वं याभी रथमावतं जिषे | याभिस्त्रिशोक उस्रिया उदाजत ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith ye made Rasā swell full with water-floods, and urged to victory the car without a horse;  Wherewith Triśoka drove forth his recovered cows,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिः सूर्यं परियाथः परावति मन्धातारं कषैत्रपत्येष्वावतम | याभिर्विप्रं पर भरद्वाजमावतं ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith ye, compass round the Sun when far away, strengthened Mandhātar in his tasks as lord of lands,  And to sage Bharadvāja gave protecting help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिर्महामतिथिग्वं कशोजुवं दिवोदासं शम्बरहत्यावतम | याभिः पूर्भिद्ये तरसदस्युमावतं ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith, when Śambara was slain, ye guarded well great Atithigva, Divodāsa, Kaśoju,  And Trasadasyu when the forts were shattered down,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिर्वम्रं विपिपानमुपस्तुतं कलिं याभिर्वित्तजानिं दुवस्यथः | याभिर्व्यश्वमुत पर्थिमावतं ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith ye honoured the great drinker Vamra, and Upastuta and Kali when he gained his wife,  And lent to Vyaśva and to Pṛthi favouring help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिर्नरा शयवे याभिरत्रये याभिः पुरा मनवे गातुमीषथुः | याभिः शारीराजतं सयूमरश्मये ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith, O Heroes, ye vouchsafed deliverance to Śayu, Atri, and to Manu long ago;  Wherewith ye shot your shafts in Syūmaraśmi's cause.—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिः पठर्वा जठरस्य मज्मनाग्निर्नादीदेच्चित इद्धो अज्मन्ना | याभिः शर्यातमवथो महाधने ताभिर.. . ||
1.112.e: Wherewith Paṭharvā, in his majesty of form, shone in his course like to a gathered kindled fire;  Wherewith ye helped Śāryāta in the mighty fray,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिरङगिरो मनसा निरण्यथो.अग्रं गछथो विवरे गोर्णसः | याभिर्मनुं शूरमिषा समावतं ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith, Aṅgirases! ye triumphed in your heart, and onward went to liberate the flood of milk;  Wherewith ye helped the hero Manu with new strength,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिः पत्नीर्विमदाय नयूहथुरा घ वा याभिररुणीरशिक्षतम | याभिः सुदास ऊहथुः सुदेव्यं ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith ye brought a wife for Vimada to wed, wherewith ye freely gave the ruddy cows away;  Wherewith ye brought the host of kind Gods to Sudās—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिः शन्ताती भवथो ददाशुषे भुज्युं याभिरवथो याभिरध्रिगुम | ओम्यावतीं सुभरां रतस्तुभं ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith ye bring great bliss to him who offers gifts, wherewith ye have protected Bhujyu, Adhrigu,  And good and gracious Subharā and Ṛtastup,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिः कर्शानुमसने दुवस्यथो जवे याभिर्यूनो अर्वन्तमावतम | मधु परियं भरथो यत सरड्भ्यस्ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith ye served Kṛśānu where the shafts were shot, and helped the young man's horse to swiftness in the race;  Wherewith ye bring delicious honey to the bees,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिर्नरं गोषुयुधं नर्षाह्ये कषेत्रस्य साता तनयस्य जिन्वथः | याभी रथानवथो याभिरर्वतस्ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith ye speed the hero as he fights for kine in hero battle, in the strife for land and sons,  Wherewith ye safely guard his horses and his car,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins with those aids.

1.112.d: याभिः कुत्समार्जुनेयं शतक्रतू पर तुर्वीतिं पर च दभीतिमावतम | याभिर्ध्वसन्तिं पुरुषन्तिमावतं ताभिर... ||
1.112.e: Wherewith ye, Lords of Hundred Powers, helped Kutsa, son of Ārjuni, gave Turvīti and Dabhīti strength,  Favoured Dhvasanti and lent Puruṣanti help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.

1.112.d: अप्नस्वतीमश्विना वाचमस्मे कर्तं नो दस्रा वर्षणा मनीषाम | अद्यूत्ये.अवसे नि हवये वां वर्धे च नो भवतं वाजसातौ ||
1.112.e: Make ye our speech effectual, O ye Aśvins, and this our hymn, ye mighty Wonder-Workers.  In luckless game I call on you for succour: strengthen us also on the field of battle.

1.112.d: दयुभिरक्तुभिः परि पातमस्मानरिष्टेभिरश्विना सौभगेभिः | तन नो ... ||
1.112.e: With, undiminished blessings, O ye Aśvins, for evermore both night and day protect us.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.113.d: इदं शरेष्ठं जयोतिषां जयोतिरागाच्चित्रः परकेतो अजनिष्ट विभ्वा | यथा परसूता सवितुः सवयमेवा रात्र्युषसे योनिमारैक ||
1.113.e: This light is come, amid all lights the fairest; born is the brilliant, far-extending brightness.  Night, sent away for Savitar's uprising, hath yielded up a birth-place for the Morning.

1.113.d: रुशद्वत्सा रुशती शवेत्यागादारैगु कर्ष्णा सदनान्यस्याः | समानबन्धू अम्र्ते अनुची दयावा वर्णं चरत आमिनाने ||
1.113.e: The Fair, the Bright is come with her white offspring; to her the Dark One hath resigned her dwelling.  Akin, immortal, following each other, changing their colours both the heavens move onward.

1.113.d: समानो अध्वा सवस्रोरनन्तस्तमन्यान्या चरतो देवशिष्टे | न मेथेते न तस्थतुः सुमेके नक्तोषासा समनसा विरूपे ||
1.113.e: Common, unending is the Sisters' pathway; taught by the Gods, alternately they travel.  Fair-formed, of different hues and yet one-minded, Night and Dawn clash not, neither do they travel.

1.113.d: भास्वती नेत्री सून्र्तानामचेति चित्रा वि दुरो न आवः | परार्प्या जगद वयु नो रायो अख्यदुषा अजीगर्भुवनानि विश्वा ||
1.113.e: Bright leader of glad sounds, our eyes behold her; splendid in hue she hath unclosed the portals.  She, stirring up the world, hath shown us riches: Dawn hath awakened every living creature.

1.113.d: जिह्मश्ये चरितवे मघोन्याभोगय इष्टये राय उ तवम | दभ्रं पश्यद्भ्य उर्विया विचक्ष उषा ||
1.113.e: Rich Dawn, she sets afoot the coiled-up sleeper, one for enjoyment, one for wealth or worship,  Those who saw little for extended vision. All living creatures hath the Dawn awakened.

1.113.d: कषत्राय तवं शरवसे तवं महीया इष्टये तवमर्थमिवत्वमित्यै | विसद्र्शा जीविताभिप्रचक्ष उषा ... ||
1.113.e: One to high sway, one to exalted glory, one to pursue his gain, and one his labour:  All to regard their different vocations, all moving creatures hath the Dawn awakened.

1.113.d: एषा दिवो दुहिता परत्यदर्शि वयुछन्ती युवतिः शुक्रवासाः | विश्वस्येशाना पार्थिवस्य वस्व उषो अद्येह सुभगेव्युछ ||
1.113.e: We see her there, the Child of Heaven apparent, the young Maid, flushing in her shining raiment.  Thou sovran Lady of all earthly treasure, flush on us here, auspicious Dawn, this morning.

1.113.d: परायतीनामन्वेति पाथ आयतीनां परथमा शश्वतीनाम | वयुछन्ती जीवमुदीरयन्त्युषा मर्तं कं चन बोधयन्ती ||
1.113.e: She first of endless morns to come hereafter, follows the path of morns that have departed.  Dawn, at her rising, urges forth the living him who is dead she wakes not from his slumber.

1.113.d: उषो यदग्निं समिधे चकर्थ वि यदावश्चक्षसा सूर्यस्य | यन मानुषान यक्ष्यमाणानजीगस्तद देवेषु चक्र्षे भद्रमप्नः ||
1.113.e: As thou, Dawn, hast caused Agni to be kindled, and with the Sun's eye hast revealed creation.  And hast awakened men to offer worship, thou hast performed, for Gods, a noble service.

1.113.d: कियात्या यत समया भवाति या वयूषुर्याश्च नूनंव्युछान | अनु पूर्वाः कर्पते वावशाना परदीध्याना जोषमन्याभिरेति ||
1.113.e: How long a time, and they shall be together,—Dawns that have shone and Dawns to shine hereafter?  She yearns for former Dawns with eager longing, and goes forth gladly shining with the others.

1.113.d: ईयुष टे ये पूर्वतरामपश्यन वयुछन्तीमुषसं मर्त्यासः | अस्माभिरू नु परतिचक्ष्याभूदो ते यन्ति ये अपरीषु पश्यान ||
1.113.e: Gone are the men who in the days before us looked on the rising of the earlier Morning.  We, we the living, now behold her brightness and they come nigh who shall hereafter see her.

1.113.d: यावयद्द्वेषा रतपा रतेजाः सुम्नावरी सून्र्ता ईरयन्ती | सुमङगलीर्बिभ्रती देववीतिमिहाद्योषः शरेष्ठतमाव्युछ ||
1.113.e: Foe-chaser, born of Law, the Law's protectress, joy-giver, waker of all pleasant voices,  Auspicious, bringing food for Gods’ enjoyment, shine on us here, most bright, O Dawn, this morning.

1.113.d: शश्वत पुरोषा वयुवास देव्यथो अद्येदं वयावो मघोनी | अथो वयुछादुत्तराननु दयूनजराम्र्ता चरति सवधाभिः ||
1.113.e: From days eternal hath Dawn shone, the Goddess, and shows this light to-day, endowed with riches.  So will she shine on days to come immortal she moves on in her own strength, undecaying.

1.113.d: वयञ्जिभिर्दिव आतास्वद्यौदप कर्ष्णां निर्णिजं देव्यावः | परबोधयन्त्यरुणेभिरश्वैरोषा याति सुयुजा रथेन ||
1.113.e: In the sky's borders hath she shone in splendour: the Goddess hath thrown off the veil of darkness.  Awakening the world with purple horses, on her well-harnessed chariot Dawn approaches.

1.113.d: आवहन्ती पोष्या वार्याणि चित्रं केतुं कर्णुते चेकिताना | ईयुषीणामुपमा शश्वतीनां विभातीनां परथमोषा वयश्वैत ||
1.113.e: Bringing all life-sustaining blessings with her, showing herself she sends forth brilliant lustre.  Last of the countless mornings that have vanished, first of bright morns to come hath Dawn arisen.

1.113.d: उदीर्ध्वं जीवो असुर्न आगादप परागात तम आ जयोतिरेति | आरैक पन्थां यातवे सूर्यायागन्म यत्र परतिरन्त आयुः ||
1.113.e: Arise! the breath, the life, again hath reached us: darkness hath passed away and light approacheth.  She for the Sun hath left a path to travel we have arrived where men prolong existence.

1.113.d: सयूमना वाच उदियर्ति वह्नि सतवानो रेभ उषसो विभातीः | अद्या तदुछ गर्णते मघोन्यस्मे आयुर्नि दिदीहि परजावत ||
1.113.e: Singing the praises of refulgent Mornings with his hymn's web the priest, the poet rises.  Shine then to-day, rich Maid, on him who lauds thee, shine down on us the gift of life and offspring.

1.113.d: या गोमतीरुषसः सर्ववीरा वयुछन्ति दाशुषे मर्त्याय | वायोरिव सून्र्तानामुदर्के ता अश्वदा अश्नवत सोमसुत्वा ||
1.113.e: Dawns giving sons all heroes, kine and horses, shining upon the man who brings oblations,—  These let the Soma-presser gain when ending his glad songs louder than the voice of Vāyu.

1.113.d: माता देवानामदितेरनीकं यज्ञस्य केतुर्ब्र्हती वि भाहि | परशस्तिक्र्द बरह्मणे नो वयुछा नो जने जनय विश्ववारे ||
1.113.e: Mother of Gods, Aditi's form of glory, ensign of sacrifice, shine forth exalted.  Rise up, bestowing praise on our devotion all-bounteous, make us chief among the people.

1.113.d: यच्चित्रमप्न उषसो वहन्तीजानाय शशमानाय भद्रम | तन नो ... ||
1.113.e: Whatever splendid wealth the Dawns bring with them to bless the man who offers praise and worship,  Even that may Mitra, Varuṇa vouchsafe us, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.114.d: इमा रुद्राय तवसे कपर्दिने कषयद्वीराय पर भरामहे मतीः | यथा शमसद दविपदे चतुष्पदे विश्वं पुष्टंग्रामे अस्मिन्ननातुरम ||
1.114.e: To the strong Rudra bring we these our songs of praise, to him the Lord of Heroes with the braided hair,  That it be well with all our cattle and our men, that in this village all be healthy and well-fed.

1.114.d: मर्ळा नो रुद्रोत नो मयस कर्धि कषयद्वीराय नमसा विधेमते | यच्छं च योश्च मनुरायेजे पिता तदश्याम तवरुद्र परणीतिषु ||
1.114.e: Be gracious unto us, O Rudra, bring us joy: thee, Lord of Heroes, thee with reverence will we serve.  Whatever health and strength our father Manu won by sacrifice may we, under thy guidance, gain.

1.114.d: अश्याम ते सुमतिं देवयज्यया कषयद्वीरस्य तव रुद्र मीढ्वः | सुम्नायन्निद विशो अस्माकमा चरारिष्टवीरा जुहवाम ते हविः ||
1.114.e: By worship of the Gods may we, O Bounteous One, O Rudra, gain thy grace, Ruler of valiant men.  Come to our families, bringing them bliss: may we, whose heroes are uninjured, bring thee sacred gifts,

1.114.d: तवेषं वयं रुद्रं यज्ञसाधं वङकुं कविमवसे निह्वयामहे | आरे अस्मद दैव्यं हेळो अस्यतु सुमतिमिद वयमस्या वर्णीमहे ||
1.114.e: Hither we call for aid the wise, the wanderer, impetuous Rudra, perfecter of sacrifice.  May he repel from us the anger of the Gods: verily we desire his favourable grace.

1.114.d: दिवो वराहमरुषं कपर्दिनं तवेषं रूपं नमसा निह्वयामहे | हस्ते बिभ्रद भेषजा वार्याणि शर्म वर्म छर्दिरस्मभ्यं यंसत ||
1.114.e: Him with the braided hair we call with reverence down, the wild-boar of the sky, the red, the dazzling shape.  May he, his hand filled full of sovran medicines, grant us protection, shelter, and a home secure.

1.114.d: इदं पित्रे मरुतामुच्यते वचः सवादोः सवादीयो रुद्राय वर्धनम | रास्वा च नो अम्र्त मर्तभोजनं तमने तोकाय तनयाय मर्ळ ||
1.114.e: To him the Maruts’ Father is this hymn addressed, to strengthen Rudra's might, a song more sweet than sweet.  Grant us, Immortal One, the food which mortals eat: be gracious unto me, my seed, my progeny.

1.114.d: मा नो महान्तमुत मा नो अर्भकं मा न उक्षन्तमुत मान उक्षितम | मा नो वधीः पितरं मोत मातरं मा नः परियास्तन्वो रुद्र रीरिषः ||
1.114.e: O Rudra, harm not either great or small of us, harm not the growing boy, harm not the full-grown man.  Slay not a sire among us, slay no mother here, and to our own dear bodies, Rudra, do not harm.

1.114.d: मा नस्तोके तनये मा न आयौ मा नो गोषु मा नो अश्वेषुरीरिषः | वीरान मा नो रुद्र भामितो वधीर्हविष्मन्तःसदमित तवा हवामहे ||
1.114.e: Harm us not, Rudra, in our seed and progeny, harm us not in the living, nor in cows or steeds,  Slay not our heroes in the fury of thy wrath. Bringing oblations evermore we call to thee.

1.114.d: उप ते सतोमान पशुपा इवाकरं रास्वा पितर्मरुतां सुम्नमस्मे | भद्रा हि ते सुमतिर्म्र्ळयत्तमाथा वयमव इत्ते वर्णीमहे ||
1.114.e: Even as a herdsman I have brought thee hymns of praise: O Father of the Maruts, give us happiness,  Blessed is thy most favouring benevolence, so, verily, do we desire thy saving help.

1.114.d: आरे ते गोघ्नमुत पूरुषघ्नं कषयद्वीर सुम्नमस्मे तेस्तु | मर्ळा च नो अधि च बरूहि देवाधा च नः शर्म यछद्विबर्हाः ||
1.114.e: Far be thy dart that killeth men or cattle: thy bliss be with us, O thou Lord of Heroes.  Be gracious unto us, O God, and bless us, and then vouchsafe us doubly-strong protection.

1.114.d: अवोचाम नमो अस्मा अवस्यवः शर्णोतु नो हवं रुद्रो मरुत्वान | तन नो ... ||
1.114.e: We, seeking help, have spoken and adored him: may Rudra, girt by Maruts, hear our calling.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.115.d: चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः | आप्रा दयावाप्र्थिवी अन्तरिक्षं सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च ||
1.115.e: THE brilliant presence of the Gods hath risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni.  The soul of all that moveth not or moveth, the Sun hath filled the air and earth and heaven.

1.115.d: सूर्यो देवीमुषसं रोचमानां मर्यो न योषामभ्येति पश्चात | यत्रा नरो देवयन्तो युगानि वितन्वते परति भद्राय भद्रम ||
1.115.e: Like as a young man followeth a maiden, so doth the Sun the Dawn, refulgent Goddess:  Where pious men extend their generations, before the Auspicious One for happy fortune.

1.115.d: भद्रा अश्वा हरितः सूर्यस्य चित्रा एतग्वा अनुमाद्यासः | नमस्यन्तो दिव आ पर्ष्ठमस्थुः परि दयावाप्र्थिवी यन्ति सद्यः ||
1.115.e: Auspicious are the Sun's Bay-coloured Horses, bright, changing hues, meet for our shouts of triumph.  Bearing our prayers, the sky's ridge have they mounted, and in a moment speed round earth and heaven.

1.115.d: तत सूर्यस्य देवत्वं तन महित्वं मध्या कर्तोर्विततं सं जभार | यदेदयुक्त हरितः सधस्थादाद रात्री वासस्तनुते सिमस्मै ||
1.115.e: This is the Godhead, this might of Sūrya: he hath withdrawn what spread o’er work unfinished.  When he hath loosed his Horses from their station, straight over all Night spreadeth out her garment.

1.115.d: तन मित्रस्य वरुणस्याभिचक्षे सूर्यो रूपं कर्णुते दयोरुपस्थे | अनन्तमन्यद रुशदस्य पाजः कर्ष्णमन्यद धरितः सं भरन्ति ||
1.115.e: In the sky's lap the Sun this form assumeth that Varuṇa and Mitra may behold it.  His Bay Steeds well maintain his power eternal, at one time bright and darksome at another.

1.115.d: अद्या देवा उदिता सूर्यस्य निरंहसः पिप्र्ता नरवद्यात | तन नो ... ||
1.115.e: This day, O Gods, while Sūrya is ascending, deliver us from trouble and dishonour.  This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

1.116.d: नासत्याभ्यां बर्हिरिव पर वर्ञ्जे सतोमानियर्म्यभ्रियेव वातः | यावर्भगाय विमदाय जायां सेनाजुवा नयूहतूरथेन ||
1.116.e: I TRIM like grass my song for the Nāsatyas and send their lauds forth as the wind drives rain-clouds,  Who, in a chariot rapid as an arrow, brought to the youthful Vimada a consort.

1.116.d: वीळुपत्मभिराशुहेमभिर्वा देवानां वा जूतिभिः शाशदाना | तद रासभो नासत्या सहस्रमाजा यमस्य परधने जिगाय ||
1.116.e: Borne on by rapid steeds of mighty pinion, or proudly trusting in the Gods’ incitements.  That stallion ass of yours won, O Nāsatyas, that thousand in the race, in Yama's contest.

1.116.d: तुग्रो ह भुज्युमश्विनोदमेघे रयिं न कश्चिन मम्र्वानवाहाः | तमूहथुर्नौभिरात्मन्वतीभिरन्तरिक्षप्रुद्भिरपोदकाभिः ||
1.116.e: Yea, Aśvins, as a dead man leaves his riches, Tugra left Bhujyu in the cloud of waters.  Ye brought him back in animated vessels, traversing air, unwetted by the billows.

1.116.d: तिस्रः कषपस्त्रिरहातिव्रजद्भिर्नासत्या भुज्युमूहथुः पतंगैः | समुद्रस्य धन्वन्नार्द्रस्य पारे तरिभी रथैः शतपद्भिः षळश्वैः ||
1.116.e: Bhujyu ye bore with winged things, Nāsatyas, which for three nights, three days full swiftly travelled,  To the sea's farther shore, the strand of ocean, in three cars, hundred-footed, with six horses.

1.116.d: अनारम्भणे तदवीरयेथामनास्थाने अग्रभणे समुद्रे | यदश्विना ऊहथुर्भुज्युमस्तं शतारित्रां नावमातस्थिवांसम ||
1.116.e: Ye wrought that hero exploit in the ocean which giveth no support, or hold or station,  What time ye carried Bhujyu to his dwelling, borne in a ship with hundred oars, O Aśvins.

1.116.d: यमश्विना ददथुः शवेतमश्वमघाश्वाय शश्वदित्स्वस्ति | तद वां दात्रं महि कीर्तेन्यं भूत पैद्वो वाजीसदमिद धव्यो अर्यः ||
1.116.e: The white horse which of old ye gave Aghāśva, Aśvins, a gift to be his wealth for ever,—  Still to be praised is that your glorious present, still to be famed is the brave horse of Pedu.
