1.164.e: The cow hath lowed after her blinking youngling; she licks his forehead, as she lows, to form it.  His mouth she fondly calls to her warm udder, and suckles him with milk while gently lowing.

1.164.d: अयं स शिङकते येन गौरभीव्र्ता मिमाति मायुं धवसनावधि शरिता | सा चित्तिभिर्नि हि चकार मर्त्यं विद्युद भवन्ती परति वव्रिमौहत ||
1.164.e: He also snorts, by whom encompassed round the Cow laws as she clings unto the shedder of the rain.  She with her shrilling cries hath humbled mortal man, and, turned to lightning, hath stripped off her covering robe.

1.164.d: अनच्छये तुरगातु जीवमेजद धरुवं मध्य आ पस्त्यानाम | जीवो मर्तस्य चरति सवधाभिरमर्त्यो मर्त्येना सयोनिः ||
1.164.e: That which hath breath and speed and life and motion lies firmly stablished in the midst of houses.  Living, by offerings to the Dead he moveth Immortal One, the brother of the mortal.

1.164.d: अपश्यं गोपामनिपद्यमानमा च परा च पथिभिश्चरन्तम | स सध्रीचीः स विशूचीर्वसान आ वरीवर्ति भुवनेष्वन्तः ||
1.164.e: I saw the Herdsman, him who never stumbles, approaching by his pathways and departing.  He, clothed with gathered and diffusive splendour, within the worlds continually travels.

1.164.d: य ईं चकार न सो अस्य वेद य ईं ददर्श हिरुगिन नुतस्मात | स मातुर्योना परिवीतो अन्तर्बहुप्रजा निर्र्तिमा विवेश ||
1.164.e: He who hath made him cloth not comprehend him: from him who saw him surely is he hidden.  He, yet enveloped in his Mother's bosom, source of much life, hath sunk into destruction.

1.164.d: दयौर्मे पिता जनिता नाभिरत्र बन्धुर्मे माता पर्थिवीमहीयम | उत्तानयोश्चम्वोर्योनिरन्तरत्रा पिता दुहितुर्गर्भमाधात ||
1.164.e: Dyaus is my Father, my begetter: kinship is here. This great earth is my kin and Mother.  Between the wide-spread world-halves is the birth-place: the Father laid the Daughter's germ within it.

1.164.d: पर्छामि तवा परमन्तं पर्थिव्याः पर्छामि यत्र भुवनस्यनाभिः | पर्छामि तवा वर्ष्णो अश्वस्य रेतः पर्छामि वाचः परमं वयोम ||
1.164.e: I ask thee of the earth's extremest limit, where is the centre of the world, I ask thee.  I ask thee of the Stallion's seed prolific, I ask of highest heaven where Speech abideth.

1.164.d: इयं वेदिः परो अन्तः पर्थिव्या अयं यज्ञो भुवनस्य नाभिः | अयं सोमो वर्ष्णो अश्वस्य रेतो बरह्मायं वाचःपरमं वयोम ||
1.164.e: This altar is the earth's extremest limit; this sacrifice of ours is the world's centre.  The Stallion's seed prolific is the Soma; this Brahman highest heaven where Speech abideth.

1.164.d: सप्तार्धगर्भा भुवनस्य रेतो विष्णोस्तिष्ठन्ति परदिशाविधर्मणि | ते धीतिभिर्मनसा ते विपश्चितः परिभुवः परि भवन्ति विश्वतः ||
1.164.e: Seven germs unripened yet are heaven's prolific seed: their functions they maintain by Viṣṇu's ordinance.  Endued with wisdom through intelligence and thought, they compass us about present on every side.

1.164.d: अन वि जानामि यदिवेदमस्मि निण्यः संनद्धो मनसा चरामि | यदा मागन परथमजा रतस्यादिद व[चो अश्नुवे भागमस्याः ||
1.164.e: What thing I truly am I know not clearly: mysterious, fettered in my mind I wander.  When the first-born of holy Law approached me, then of this speech I first obtain a portion.

1.164.d: अपां परां एति सवधया गर्भीतो.अमर्त्यो मर्त्येना सयोनिः | ता शश्वन्ता विषूचीना वियन्ता नयन्यं चिक्युर्न निचिक्युरन्यम ||
1.164.e: Back, forward goes he, grasped by strength inherent, the Immortal born the brother of the mortal  Ceaseless they move in opposite directions: men mark the one, and fail to mark the other.

1.164.d: रचो अक्षरे परमे वयोमन यस्मिन देवा अधि विश्वे निषेदुः | यस्तन न वेद किं रचा करिष्यति य इत तद विदुस्त इमे समासते ||
1.164.e: Upon what syllable of holy praise-song, as twere their highest heaven, the Gods repose them,—  Who knows not this, what will he do with praise-song? But they who know it well sit here assembled.

1.164.d: सूयवसाद भगवती हि भूया अथो वयं भगवन्तः सयाम | अद्धि तर्णमघ्न्ये विश्वदानीं पिब शुद्धमुदकमाचरन्ती ||
1.164.e: Fortunate  mayst thou be with goodly pasture, and may we also be exceeding wealthy.  Feed on the grass, O Cow, at every season, and coming hitherward drink limpid water.

1.164.d: गौरीर्मिमाय सलिलानि तक्षत्येकपदी दविपदी सा चतुष्पदी | अष्टापदी नवपदी बभूवुषी सहस्राक्षरा परमे वयोमन ||
1.164.e: Forming the water-floods, the buffalo hath lowed, one-footed or two-footed or four-footed, she,  Who hath become eight-footed or hath got nine feet, the thousand-syllabled in the sublimest heaven.

1.164.d: तस्याः समुद्रा अधि वि कषरन्ति तेन जीवन्ति परदिशश्चतस्रः | ततः कषरत्यक्षरं तद विश्वमुप जीवति ||
1.164.e: From her descend in streams the seas of water; thereby the world's four regions have their being,  Thence flows the imperishable flood and thence the universe hath life.

1.164.d: शकमयं धूममारादपश्यं विषूवता पर एनावरेण | उक्षाणं पर्श्निमपचन्त वीरास्तानि धर्माणि परथमान्यासन ||
1.164.e: I saw from far away the smoke of fuel with spires that rose on high o’er that beneath it.  The Mighty Men have dressed the spotted bullock. These were the customs in the days aforetime,

1.164.d: तरयः केशिन रतुथा वि चक्षते संवत्सरे वपत एक एषाम | विश्वमेको अभि चष्टे शचीभिर्ध्राजिरेकस्य दद्र्शेन रूपम ||
1.164.e: Three with long tresses show in ordered season. One of them sheareth when the year is ended.  One with his powers the universe regardeth: Of one, the sweep is seen, but his figure.

1.164.d: चत्वारि वाक परिमिता पदानि तानि विदुर्ब्राह्मणा ये मनीषिणः | गुहा तरीणि निहिता नेङगयन्ति तुरीयं वाचो मनुष्या वदन्ति ||
1.164.e: Speech hath been measured out in four divisions, the Brahmans who have understanding know them.  Three kept in close concealment cause no motion; of speech, men speak only the fourth division.

1.164.d: इन्द्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमाहुरथो दिव्यः स सुपर्णो गरुत्मान | एकं सद विप्रा बहुधा वदन्त्यग्निं यमं मातरिश्वानमाहुः ||
1.164.e: They call him Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, and he is heavenly nobly-winged Garutmān.  To what is One, sages give many a title they call it Agni, Yama, Mātariśvan.

1.164.d: कर्ष्णं नियानं हरयः सुपर्णा अपो वसाना दिवमुत पतन्ति | त आवव्र्त्रन सदनाद रतस्यादिद घर्तेन पर्थिवी वयुद्यते ||
1.164.e: Dark the descent: the birds are golden-coloured; up to the heaven they fly robed in the waters.  Again descend they from the seat of Order, and all the earth is moistened with their fatness.

1.164.d: दवादश परधयश्चक्रमेकं तरीणि नभ्यानि क उ तच्चिकेत | तस्मिन साकं तरिशता न शङकवो.अर्पिताः षष्टिर्न चलाचलासः ||
1.164.e: Twelve are the fellies, and the wheel is single; three are the naves. What man hath understood it?  Therein are set together spokes three hundred and sixty, which in nowise can be loosened.

1.164.d: यस्ते सतनः शशयो यो मयोभूर्येन विश्वा पुष्यसि वार्याणि | यो रत्नधा वसुविद यः सुदत्रः सरस्वति तमिह धातवे कः ||
1.164.e: That breast of thine exhaustless, spring of pleasure, wherewith thou feedest all things that are choicest,  Wealth-giver, treasure. finder, free bestower,—bring that, Sarasvatī, that we may drain it.

1.164.d: यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजन्त देवास्तनि धर्माणि परथमान्यासन | ते ह नाकं महिमानः सचन्त यत्र पूर्वे साध्याः सन्ति देवाः ||
1.164.e: By means of sacrifice the Gods accomplished their sacrifice: these were the earliest ordinances.  These Mighty Ones attained the height of heaven, there where the Sādhyas, Gods of old, are dwelling.

1.164.d: समानमेतदुदकमुच्चैत्यव चाहभिः | भूमिं पर्जन्या जिन्वन्ति दिवं जिन्वन्त्यग्नयः ||
1.164.e: Uniform, with the passing days, this water mounts and fails again.  The tempest-clouds give life to earth, and fires re-animate the heaven.

1.164.d: दिव्यं सुपर्णं वायसं बर्हन्तमपां गर्भं दर्शतमोषधीनाम | अभीपतो वर्ष्टिभिस्तर्पयन्तं सरस्वन्तमवसे जोहवीमि ||
1.164.e: The Bird Celestial, vast with noble pinion, the lovely germ of plants, the germ of waters,  Him who delighteth us with rain in season, Sarasvān I invoke that he may help us.
